An unknown investor has built a position in Zcash (ZEC) worth about $14 million, splitting the capital between the spot market and the decentralized derivatives exchange Hyperliquid. The purchases came amid preparations for the Network Upgrade 7 (NU7) hard fork: on November 5, it is set to speed up block processing threefold.

Judging by on-chain data, the address t1JJnA linked to the investor first bought 3,052 ZEC (about $3.8 million) on the spot market at an average price of $1,250. Then, on Hyperliquid, it opened a 2x leveraged long on 8,000 ZEC worth $10.16 million in two different wallets.

So far, 3,000 ZEC of this position can be verified, with an average entry price of $1,353.83.

In late October, ZEC pulled back to the $1,220–$1,280 range, and the derivatives position went into the red. At its peak, the paper loss exceeded $1.8 million; it now stands at $249,388.

But liquidation will only occur if the price falls to $647.67, which is nearly half of current levels. The investor is clearly betting on long-term growth rather than a quick rebound.

The main argument is the NU7 hard fork, whose final tests the developers completed on the testnet in October. The ZIP-218 update will cut block time from 75 to 25 seconds: the network’s throughput will triple, while the issuance schedule will remain the same.

Along with the hard fork, the Network Sustainability Mechanism (a reserve fee fund for miners) will go live, and the outdated Sprout pool will be shut down in favor of the shielded Orchard architecture.

Throughout 2026, each new Zcash low came in higher than the previous one. An ascending triangle has formed on the chart, and time after time the price runs into resistance at $1,396. Traders on the derivatives market have split into two camps.

Some expect a sharp upside breakout amid inflows into the Grayscale Zcash Trust. Others fear that right after the upgrade activates on November 5, the “buy the rumor, sell the news” principle will kick in.

#5208. 'My Workouts Stopped Working in Midlife. These 8 Lessons Helped Me Get Back on Track'

Coach Michaela Bentley shares these hard-earned lessons transformed her approach to strength, nutrition, and healthy aging.

At 60, Michaela Bentley knows exactly how to train, eat and recover. But that wasn't always the case.

“As someone who's always maintained a pretty high level of fitness, that all came to a crashing halt in my late 40s,” the personal trainer and nutrition coach, who specializes in women's midlife fitness, wrote on Instagram.

“I started packing on the pounds, and all the things I had done my entire life to stay fit stopped working,” she recalled. “I was putting on weight and couldn't figure out why since I was doing the same things I'd always done.”

Here, Bentley shares what she learned from navigating those changes, while Sarah Campus, personal trainer, instructor, nutrition coach, and founder of LDN MUMS FITNESS, adds her expert perspective.

Effective training can be pretty boring—and that's okay. You don't need a completely different workout every time you train.

Repeating key movements allows you to practice technique, build strength, and track progression, both experts say.

“If you're doing completely different workouts every week, you're not building strength,” says Bentley.

“Constantly changing everything makes it much harder to see whether you're actually getting stronger,” agrees Campus.

There is no magic number of reps that suddenly makes a workout effective, whether that's eight, 10, or 12.

“What matters more is that you are challenging your muscles and working with enough effort to create a stimulus,” says Campus. Your final few reps should feel difficult and bring you close to failure while still allowing you to maintain good technique.

Make sure your training also becomes more challenging over time, Bentley adds, by gradually increasing the weight, reps or training volume—otherwise known as progressive overload.

Doing random workouts can keep you active, but they'll usually deliver random results.

“A structured program gives your training purpose and allows for progressive overload,” Campus says.

In midlife, consistency and progression are far more valuable than constantly chasing the latest fitness trend, which may even increase your risk of injury, she adds.

Bentley recommends sticking with a program for at least six months to a year.

Particularly if fat loss is your goal, increasing your Non-Exercise Activity Thermogenesis—or NEAT—can help reduce body fat.

NEAT includes everyday movement such as housework, walking, carrying shopping, gardening, taking the stairs instead of the elevator, and even fidgeting.

Walking, in particular, is one of the “most underrated tools for fat loss,” says Bentley.

“It increases daily energy expenditure without adding a ton of fatigue or interfering with recovery.”

“You don't have to spend hours in the gym to increase your daily energy expenditure,” Campus adds. “Taking the stairs, playing with your children or simply breaking up long periods of sitting all count.”

Your training only works if your body has the opportunity to recover and adapt.

“More training isn't always better, especially when life is already demanding,” says Campus. “Prioritize sleep, rest days, nutrition and lighter sessions when needed.”

Bentley also recommends resting for at least two minutes between challenging sets so you can perform at your best.

Consistent habits over weeks and months matter far more than one meal or one day.

“A meal out, birthday cake, or a weekend treat isn't going to undo weeks of regular training and healthy eating habits,” Campus says. “The goal is balance, not perfection.”

Bentley agrees, urging women to “eat the pizza” and “enjoy dinner with your friends.” Have fun, she says, then simply “get back to your usual routine” without dwelling on it.

It's rare to feel motivated all the time, but you don't need to, say both experts.

Building habits and routines that fit around your life—and sticking with them even when motivation dips—is a much more reliable approach.

“For fat loss, your overall calorie intake matters more than obsessing over whether those calories came from carbs or fat,” says Bentley.

When considering macros, she says to focus on food in this order: calories first, followed by protein and fiber.

Campus agrees. “Energy balance is important, but that doesn't mean calories are the only thing worth considering,” she says. “Protein, fiber, food quality, portion sizes, sleep, and activity all influence how sustainable your diet feels and how well you can stick to it.”

Kate puts together fitness content that covers functional and strength training, cardio, workout challenges, interviews and news. She's often doing gym laundry or listening to music.

Sarah Campus is a highly qualified women's PT, Nutrition Coach, Running Coach, Distance Runner, mum of 3 and founder of LDN MUMS FITNESS.

She's the host of the Soho House Run Club in Chiswick and a STRAVA and TOMMY's marathon coach and ambassador. She specialises helping non-runners get into competitive distance running.

As a fitness and holistic wellness expert, Sarah regularly features on TV and in Magazines, offering tips and advice to keep the whole family healthy and active.

Binance has published its latest Proof of Reserves report as of October 31, 2026. Judging by it, client funds are still fully backed — despite the largest hack in crypto history at the end of the month. Coverage for XRP is 100.99%, and for the Ripple USD (RLUSD) stablecoin, 100.83%.

A comparison of balances as of October 1 and October 31 shows how the exchange's liabilities and reserves changed after the October 29 attack: hackers then withdrew about $6.3 billion from its wallets across ten blockchains.

Immediately after the attack, Binance suspended withdrawals and deposits, so the growth of balances in Ripple assets occurred before the hack. October results:

The main thing in the report is something else: Binance confirmed full coverage of the ten most traded assets, including BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB and SOL — and did so just two days after the hack.

About $3 billion of the stolen funds was quickly frozen directly on the blockchains with the help of partners, including Tether, Circle and Ripple. To cover the losses and return reserves to 1:1, Binance allocated more than $6.34 billion of its own capital. This reserve included the SAFU fund, the Binance Futures insurance fund and retained earnings.

The remaining 5% of losses are in low-liquidity tokens: they are being quietly bought back through over-the-counter (OTC) desks so as not to crash spot prices.

Each client can verify their own balance: the report is built on Merkle trees and zero-knowledge proofs (zk-SNARKs). For the market, this case sets a new bar: an exchange is no longer judged by whether it gets hacked, but by how quickly it stops an attack and whether it has enough of its own money to plug the hole.

#5205. Morning Minute: Binance’s $6.4B Hack Overshadows Hyperliquid’s Biggest Day

Morning Minute: Binance’s $6.4B Hack Overshadows Hyperliquid’s Biggest Day

Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.

Someone stole about $6.4 billion from Binance. That is, by a wide margin, the biggest crypto theft that has ever happened, four times the $1.5 billion taken from Bybit in February 2025.

The money left across three different blockchains: roughly $3.5 billion in ETH, $1.4 billion in BTC, and $630 million on Tron (final accounting still underway).

Luckily, stablecoin issuers can freeze their own tokens; it’s a kill switch built into USDT and USDC. Tether and Circle used it, locking up about $2.39 billion between them. That’s 43% of the haul. That leaves somewhere between $2.6 and $3.2 billion still out there.

Aave also stepped in, freezing its V3 and V4 markets on Ethereum. That’s precautionary, given the worry is an attacker using stolen money to borrow against and leave the protocol holding bad debt.

As this was playing out, Binance stated it’s “aware of reports of a potential security issue” and that user funds are “completely safe,” and paused withdrawals on multiple networks. The clearest comment came from CZ, who no longer runs Binance but is its largest shareholder: it “does look like a hack,” and he expects user funds to be “fully covered.” Later in the evening, Binance announced that it has reserved over $6.34B in company funds to cover losses. So funds are indeed “safu.”

ZachXBT shared that the Binance hack funds were commingled with funds from the $388M Bitget exploit, leading him to believe it’s the same hacker group out of North Korea behind the attack. As for how it happened, Binance pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop which was compromised, allowing the attacks to submit the unauthorized transactions, before identifying "additional points of breach" in the following hours.

Markets did what you’d expect. Bitcoin fell below $797,000, ETH fell sub-$2,200 and BNB sub-$700. Over $1.33B in positions got liquidated on the day.

Unfortunately, this came after what was shaping up to be one of the most positive days for a crypto project in its history.

Earlier on Thursday, Trade.xyz announced that Intercontinental Exchange (the company that owns the New York Stock Exchange) is investing in it. The plan is a regulated U.S. venue offering round-the-clock perpetual futures built on Hyperliquid: stocks, indices, commodities, currencies and crypto, with its own exchange and clearing setup, pending CFTC approval.

Stanley Druckenmiller is joining as well, the first of a small group of outside market figures. He already owns the trade; his family office disclosed a $23 million position in Hyperliquid Strategies earlier this year.

So Hyperliquid has its path to a fully regulated perps offering inside the U.S., claims Stanley Druckenmiller as an investor (and a tout on X), and ICE’s CEO said that Hyperliquid was “bigger than NASDAQ.” Doesn’t get much better than that.

I am excited to be an investor in trade(xyz) as they partner with ICE to bring 24/7 perpetual futures on Hyperliquid to the United States. As a market participant, I am looking forward to to using their innovative product to enhance my investment process.

— Stan Druckenmiller (@standuquesne) October 29, 2026

HYPE shot as high as $97 on the day, up more than 20% at peak, before falling to $89 in the Binance hack aftermath. As of this morning, it’s at $93 and still up 8% on the day.

Unfortunately, now we have to deal with the Binance hack aftermath. Hyperliquid is a likely winner as a primary DEX option vs CEXs like Binance (which will likely be less trusted now.) But there’s also a good chance of the entire market being dragged down by fears of more exploits looming.

We will find out soon enough. Expect a bumpy ride…

#5204. Cardano Foundation Joins Swiss CMTA. ADA Tests $0.20

Home » Cardano (ADA) » Cardano Foundation Joins Swiss CMTA. ADA Tests $0.20

Cardano Foundation just opened the path for multi-billion tokenized shares on the mainstream Layer-1 network.

The Cardano Foundation has joined Switzerland’s Capital Markets and Technology Association, and the group has recognized Cardano’s CIP-0113 programmable token standard as equivalent to its own CMTAT framework for certifying tokenized shares.

The move advances regulated securities tokenization on the network at the same time ADA trades in a clear bearish structure and tests the $0.182 area.

The Foundation announced membership in CMTA on October 29. CMTA is the Swiss industry association that develops practical standards for issuing and managing securities on distributed ledgers.

Following the mainnet launch of CIP-0113 earlier in the month, CMTA’s Expert Committee treated a reviewed Cardano implementation of the standard as technically equivalent to CMTAT for equity securities.

NEW: Cardano Foundation joins CMTA, the Swiss entity "setting the standard for tokenized capital markets," alongside members including UBS, with $7T in AUM. CMTA has recognized $ADA's CIP-113 as "equivalent to the CMTAT—meaning issuers can use it to tokenize certifiable shares." pic.twitter.com/iqmz811b4U

Issuers that meet the deployment conditions can therefore use it to tokenize shares that are eligible for CMTA’s certification process.

CIP-0113 went live on Cardano’s (ADA) mainnet on October 7 without a hard fork. It lets issuers attach compliance rules.

KYC and AML checks, sanctions screening, freeze and seize powers, and transfer restrictions, directly to native Cardano tokens. The ledger enforces those rules on every transfer, mint, or burn.

The blokchain recognition is limited to tokenized shares (equity), does not extend to tokenized debt or Cardano’s base-layer infrastructure, and still requires each issuance to satisfy Swiss legal and technical checks.

Shortly after launch, Veridian, a digital-identity company spun out from the Foundation, tokenized its own shares as ledger-based securities under Switzerland’s DLT Act using the standard, becoming the first publicly identified issuer to do so.

While the institutional groundwork advances, ADA’s chart tells a different short-term story. On the 4-hour timeframe the token continues a downtrend of lower highs and lower lows. It has slipped below the $0.20 support zone and is testing the $0.182 area.

$ADA / USDT – 4HCardano continues trading in a strong bearish downtrend with lower highs and lower lows 👀📉ADA has slipped below the $0.20 support zone and is now testing $0.182. Buyers need to step in quickly to prevent further downside.🎯 Bullish recovery target: $0.2188… pic.twitter.com/VVA9FFVh1W

A reclaim of $0.20 is widely viewed as the first requirement for any shift in near-term sentiment, with resistance levels clustered around 0.2004–0.2188.

Until that reclaim occurs, bears remain in control and further downside remains possible if buyers fail to defend the current zone.

The CMTA membership and CIP-0113 equivalence give Cardano a clearer route into regulated tokenized capital markets in Switzerland, where ledger-based securities already have a defined legal framework. MSB Intel says the opportunities are in the trillions.

The Cardano Foundation has joined CMTA, the Swiss body that sets tokenized securities standards, whose members include UBS, Pictet and Lombard Odier.UBS alone has $7.328T in invested assets.@Cardano pic.twitter.com/Vb4bVAac0X

No doubt, this is the kind of standard work that makes real-world assets (RWAs) practical rather than purely experimental.

At the same time, the token’s price continues to reflect broader market weakness, with ADA trading near $0.19 and still well below prior cycle levels. For now the institutional plumbing is moving forward even as the chart remains under pressure.

#5203. This Woman Lifted Weights 5 Times a Week for 4 Weeks—Here’s How Her Body Changed

Makari Espe swapped two 20-min weights sessions a week for five 30-min sessions—and documented the results.

If ever you’ve wondered exactly what upping the amount of weight training you do could do for your body, let Canadian YouTuber Makari Espe’s story give you an idea. Already accustomed to 20-minute strength sessions twice a week, she committed to five 30-minute workouts every week for four weeks. The aim? To become “harder, better, faster, and stronger.”

To put her results to the test, she recorded her strength before and after the challenge, from how long she could hold a plank to how many chin-ups and push-ups she could do. Along the way, she also documented the reality of training five days a week on her YouTube channel. By the end of those 28 days, she wasn’t just feeling stronger—she could perform more reps, hold exercises for longer, and lift heavier weights. Here’s what happened.

“My current weightlifting routine is 20 minutes a day, two times per week, but I want to be harder, better, faster, and stronger. So, for the next month, I'm going to lift weights five times a week for 30 minutes.”

“Basically, the idea is to do two big muscle groups per workout so that each muscle group is rested by the time you work it out again and we're not all out here hating our lives. For example, it’s 7:00 in the morning and today we're going to be doing back and biceps. Tomorrow I'll be doing legs and shoulders, and then day three is a rest day.”

“I didn't come up with this routine by myself, by the way. I'm not a personal trainer and I'm very lazy when it comes to planning my own workouts. I wish this was a sponsor, but it's not. I'm just here to tell you that I'm getting all of my workouts from the Peloton app. Woo! This week I'll be doing the beginner 5-day program, and for the next 3 weeks I'll be doing these intermediate programs.”

Espe performed a baseline strength test at the start of her 28-day challenge and the same test at the end of the 28 days. She recorded the following results:

Before:1:30 plank / 1-minute wall sit / 2 chin-ups / 10 push-ups / 25 × 10-lb shoulder presses.

After four weeks:2-minute plank / 2-minute wall sit / 4 chin-ups / 15 push-ups / 25 × 15-lb shoulder presses.

As Espe’s body got used to the change in training frequency, she noticed her soreness increased. That post-workout pain has a name: delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS), the stiffness and tenderness that can kick in a day or two after a challenging or unfamiliar session as your muscles repair and adapt.

By week two, she said, “My triceps are killing me more so than any other muscle group this whole challenge so far, my body is sore in many places and I'm very tired.” She added that her hamstrings were “so sore” and her “legs hurt so bad.” By week three, she said, “The place where it hurts right now is my shoulder blades; it feels like somebody hit me with a hammer.”

The DOMS might have intensified, but she did work out an effective salve: active recovery. For Espe, that meant gentle cycling, swimming, and stretching, which helped increase blood flow to the sore areas and to ease the stiffness without adding to her training load.

She said: “It's 7:30 a.m. and I just went for a bike ride and now I'm going to go for a swim. I've been wanting to do that every day this week and I finally did it, and it was glorious. Best morning ever. And now I'm going to go stretch. The swim was amazing for many reasons, but the main one was it was so nice on my sore muscles.”

She didn’t set out with aesthetic goals, and it was her performance that really improved. On week three, she said: “I've crossed the threshold and I’ve found the joy in weightlifting again. I'm doing it because I know I can and I'm super strong. I just feel really strong and that's awesome.” A week later, by week four, she added, “I actually feel even stronger than I did as a teenager.”

As her fatigue increased in those initial weeks, by week three, she decided to take stock of what she was putting into her body—and her energy soared: “I'm putting so much more good fuel into my body which is giving me more energy to perform in the gym,” she said.

As the challenge came to an end, she noticed that her mindset had improved as well as her physical strength. “This is going to sound really cheesy, but it's because not only do I feel physically stronger, but I feel stronger in my brain. Like, I feel like I'm more resilient for having been able to push through all of the self-doubt,” she said.

“I will say that roughly 3 and 1/2 hours every week is a lot of free time to be able to put towards working out, but ultimately it makes me feel so much better outside of the gym, and that's kind of why I do all this.”

“So if you decide to do a challenge like this, absolutely take pride in your physical accomplishments, but please be sure to notice the benefits outside of the gym too.”

As Women’s Health UK’s fitness director and a qualified Pilates and yoga instructor, Bridie Wilkins has been passionately reporting on exercise, health and nutrition since the start of her decade-long career in journalism.

After earning a first-class degree in journalism and NCTJ accreditation, she secured her first role at Look Magazine, where she launched the magazine’s health and fitness column, Look Fit, before going on to become Health and Fitness writer at HELLO!

Since, she has written for Stylist, Glamour, Cosmopolitan, Marie Claire, Elle, The Metro, Runner’s World and Red. Today, she oversees all fitness content across Women's Health online and in print, spearheading leading cross-platform franchises, such as ‘Fit At Any Age’, which showcases the women proving that age is no barrier to exercise.

She has also represented the brand on BBC Radio London, plus various podcasts and Substacks – all with the aim to encourage more women to exercise and show them how. Outside of work, find her trying the latest Pilates studio, testing her VO2 max for fun (TY, Oura), or posting workouts on Instagram.

The YouTube video does not supply the starting daily transaction count, limiting what that growth multiple says about sustained adoption.

Linda reports that Solana’s Alpenglow upgrade is live on mainnet beta, citing a reduction in finality from roughly 12.8 seconds to 150 milliseconds. Those figures imply about an 85-fold improvement, rather than the approximately 40-fold increase stated in the narration.

For Cardano, she describes Leios as approaching rollout through the Dijkstra hard fork, with initial throughput expected at three to five times current levels and later improvements targeting 10–15 times. These remain forward-looking claims in the video, not demonstrated performance results.

#5198. Solana Officially Scores 1,000 Days Without Outage

The Solana network has hit a significant milestone in its quest to overcome its early hurdles, successfully going 1,000 days without a network-wide outage.

This feat stands in stark contrast to Solana's past, when the blockchain experienced some notable network disruptions. One of the more significant outages occurred in September 2021, when a spike in bot traffic from Grape Protocol IDO transactions led to a surge in transactions that overwhelmed validators and hindered consensus, resulting in a roughly 17-hour network outage.

The Solana network experienced similar problems in April 2022, with a large traffic spike due to an NFT mint that led to a roughly 7-hour outage. Another outage happened in June 2022, when a bug involving durable nonce transactions caused block production to stop for roughly 4.5 hours. Finally, in September 2022, the network experienced a fork due to a bug in the consensus layer, which led to a halt in block production lasting over 6 hours.

The final major outage occurred back in February 2023, when abnormal block forwarding overwhelmed Solana's Turbine block propagation system, leaving validators stuck in a vote-only state and leading to a coordinated restart. This would prove to be a monumental event for Solana in terms of its engineering progress.

Solana has seen a string of updates and engineering innovations by its developers in an effort to improve the network's ability to avoid the failures that had plagued it in the past. Some of these features include stake-weighted quality of service to better prioritize traffic from staked validators. The network also saw networking innovations such as QUIC that provide more flexibility in dealing with spam and congestion. There have also been updates to deduplication logic following the February 2023 outage. Additionally, the network has seen innovations such as a local fee market and other scheduling improvements to discourage users and bots from spamming the network with duplicate transactions.

Recently, Solana has emphasized that network resilience should be taken seriously. In a September 2026 update, the project shared that the network has seen 100% uptime since February 2024 and has continued to handle large amounts of traffic. It also highlighted a major infrastructure provider experiencing a routing failure in August 2026 that caused validators representing nearly 29% of the network's stake to go offline, but this did not result in a halt in block production. The project uses this as an example of increased fault tolerance.

For Solana, this 1,000-day milestone is not just a success in terms of network uptime. It's a statement and a demonstration to the world that a network once mocked for outages can now support serious financial and on-chain use cases.

#5197. The Brooks Running Shoes to Power Your Soccer Training

Find the right pair for sprint work, endurance runs, and active recovery days.

Anyone who’s ever huffed and puffed their way through a pickup soccer game after not playing for a while knows how quickly the sport can expose your conditioning. A match requires repeated bursts of speed with few opportunities to catch your breath, making stamina essential from the first minute through the 90th or beyond.

The average elite soccer player covers about 6.4 miles per game. But even if you’re just a weekend rec-leaguer, cross-training can help you cover more ground without fading late in the match. Running—including sprints, endurance work, and easy jogs—should be a regular part of your routine, and the right shoes can help you get more out of every workout.

Not sure which pair you need? Brooks—a leader in performance running shoes—offers an option for every type of run. Whether you’re doing sprint repeats, heading out for a 10K, or keeping things easy on an off day, here’s how to choose the right model for your workout.

You know what you don’t want to think about when you’re doing sprint drills? Your feet—or at least how your feet feel in your shoes. During workouts built around acceleration and all-out speed, you need a shoe that delivers support, flexibility, and comfort. For the Glycerin Flex, that’s check, check, and check.

Support comes in the form of Brooks’ proprietary nitrogen-infused DNA TUNED midsole foam, which features large cells in the heel to cushion your landings and smaller cells in the forefoot for responsive toe-offs. The combination helps you land comfortably and push off with power as you pick up the pace.

For sprint work, you also need a shoe that moves with you. The Glycerin Flex’s FlexZone technology combines a midfoot flex groove with a podular forefoot design to provide flexibility and support where you need it. A thin layer of sticky rubber on the outsole adds traction as you work on your speed.

You cover plenty of ground every time you take the field for a practice or match, making endurance work essential if you want to keep going through the final whistle. Longer runs can have a place in your conditioning on the days you aren’t wearing your cleats, as long as you build gradually and don’t overdo the mileage.

That’s where the Brooks Ghost Amp comes in. This new take on the brand’s popular Ghost model combines comfort with an energized ride for days when you want to take on a few more miles. Key among its features is SpringRamp forefoot technology, which helps you push off the balls of your feet with a little extra oomph.

Also new is the shoe’s nitrogen-infused DNA HYPE cushioning, which combines two types of foam: lightweight PEBA, which provides high energy return and a springy feel, and EVA, which offers cushioning and stability. Together, they deliver a balance of softness and responsiveness.

Up top, the lightweight warp-knit upper provides breathability and comfort, with enough structure to help secure your foot when you pick up the pace. The eye-catching color options add a little more personality to your training miles.

Recovery days are an essential part of any athlete’s training, especially soccer players. An easy walk or jog can help you stay loose, ease stiffness, and give your mind and body a reset.

But slowing the pace doesn’t mean forgetting about your footwear. On active recovery days, you still want a shoe that provides support and keeps you comfortable. The Glycerin Max 2 does both. Though it’s also built for longer runs, this plush shoe is a natural fit for easier days.

The defining feature of the Glycerin Max 2 is its dramatic GlideRoll Rocker technology. Its sculpted bevel and toe spring help your foot move smoothly from heel to toe. The shoe also features a high stack of DNA TUNED foam, which provides generous cushioning underfoot to keep your legs feeling fresh and protect your body against impact.

Active recovery may not directly put the ball in the net, but the work you do between matches can help you feel ready for the next one. And the right shoe can make that work more comfortable.

#5196. Israel Extradites Alleged Nomad Bridge Exploiter to US Over $2.8M Theft: Report

Israel Extradites Alleged Nomad Bridge Exploiter to US Over $2.8M Theft: Report

Israel has extradited an Israeli-Russian citizen to the United States to face charges over the alleged theft of about $2.8 million from crypto bridge Nomad, Israel's State Attorney's Office announced on Thursday, according to a report in The Jerusalem Post.

Alexander Block, formerly known as Alexander Gurevich, was transferred to U.S. authorities early Thursday after unsuccessful appeals in Israel. He was arrested at Ben Gurion Airport in May 2025 while preparing to fly to Russia, shortly after changing his surname and obtaining a passport in his new name.

A federal grand jury in the Northern District of California indicted Block in August 2023 on four counts of computer fraud, one count of transporting stolen property and three counts of money laundering, according to Israel's Supreme Court judgment in the case. The U.S. requested his extradition in December 2024.

According to the U.S. extradition request, as set out in the judgment, a June 2022 software update left a flaw in Nomad's smart contracts that let users receive tokens on one blockchain without locking up the equivalent assets on another. Block, operating under the username "Bitlik," allegedly made six test transfers before carrying out four main transfers around August 1, 2022, receiving tokens worth more than $2.8 million. He then allegedly moved the tokens through several wallets and converted them into other cryptocurrencies to conceal their origin.

His actions exposed the flaw to other Nomad users, who drained a Nomad-controlled wallet holding more than $186 million in user funds, the request alleges. A few days later, Block returned some of the tokens and contacted a senior Nomad official on Telegram, offering to return the rest in exchange for payment for finding the flaw. He later cut off contact, and Nomad went to U.S. law enforcement.

The Jerusalem District Court approved Block's extradition in July 2025. On appeal, he argued that the transactions used functions available within Nomad's automated system, and that the public record of blockchain transfers undermined the money laundering allegations.

The Supreme Court rejected both arguments, holding that exploiting a programming flaw could constitute unlawful computer intrusion even where the software technically permitted the action, The Jerusalem Post reported. It also found that publicly visible transactions do not necessarily identify the people behind wallets or rule out efforts to conceal where funds came from.

Supreme Court President Isaac Amit later rejected Block's request for a further hearing, according to the State Attorney's Office.

The August 2022 exploit drained Nomad of nearly all its funds. Because it took little technical knowledge to copy the original attack, Paradigm researcher Sam Sun likened what followed to "a frenzied free-for-all," Decrypt reported at the time.

In December 2025, the Federal Trade Commission proposed a settlement with Illusory Systems, Nomad's operator, saying the bridge lost $186 million after hackers exploited a poorly tested software update. The settlement would require the company to return recovered funds to users who have not been reimbursed. Nomad recovered about $22 million in the days after the hack.

#5191. Hong Kong takes tokenized settlement to 24/7, plans stablecoin trials

The HKMA plans to bring regulated stablecoins into tokenized government debt trials, while HSBC says its RedCoin stablecoin has reached 50,000 users.

Hong Kong has expanded its Project Ensemble pilot to allow round-the-clock settlement of tokenized transactions, as the city’s monetary regulator prepares to bring regulated stablecoins into trials involving tokenized government debt.

On Monday, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) said that it had advanced its EnsembleTX project to a new stage allowing 24/7 real-value transactions. The HKMA said the update would help banks and their clients move funds globally, manage tokenized investments and handle treasury operations outside conventional settlement hours.

Participating banks initially settled payments through Hong Kong’s existing dollar settlement system, which limited settlement hours. When the pilot began real-value trials in November 2025, the HKMA said it planned to introduce tokenized central bank money to allow settlement around the clock.

The HKMA launched Project Ensemble in March 2024 to explore how banks could settle tokenized transactions using wholesale central bank digital money. A sandbox opened that August, allowing banks to connect their tokenized deposit platforms and test transactions.

Speaking at Hong Kong FinTech Week on Monday, HKMA Chief Executive Eddie Yue said the regulator was introducing tokenized central bank money as a “foundation layer” for 24/7 settlement. He said tokenized bonds, money market funds and bank deposits were already being used.

The HKMA also said recognized dealers had completed secondary-market trial trades in tokenized Exchange Fund Bills, a form of short-term debt issued by the regulator. It plans to expand those trials to include regulated stablecoins.

Separately, HSBC Group CEO Georges Elhedery said at Hong Kong FinTech Week that the bank’s recently launched Hong Kong dollar stablecoin, RedCoin, had reached 50,000 users about 10 days after its debut.

“We have 50,000 users,” Elhedery said, adding that HSBC was targeting “multi-million users” as it expands access to the token.

RedCoin’s rollout brings stablecoins to retail payments, while Ensemble’s settlement work has focused on transactions involving banks and tokenized investments.

Elhedery said HSBC was also offering tokenized deposits to wholesale clients in Hong Kong and about half a dozen other jurisdictions, allowing funds to move around the clock.

Related: Hong Kong prepares banks for quantum threats amid tokenization push

The bank launched RedCoin on Oct. 23 for transfers and merchant payments through its PayMe application. HSBC said more than 3.3 million PayMe customers could activate stablecoin wallets to use the token. It also plans to bring the stablecoin into its mobile banking app and allow subscriptions to tokenized investments, including a Hong Kong dollar money market fund share class.

HSBC was among Hong Kong’s first licensed stablecoin issuers in April alongside Anchorpoint Financial, a venture backed by Animoca Brands and Standard Chartered. The city’s licensing regime, introduced in August 2025, requires issuers to meet standards for backing reserves, redemption and risk management.

AI crypto trading bots help traders automate strategies, analyze market data, and manage trade execution without monitoring charts around the clock. However, not every crypto trading bot marketed as AI-powered uses artificial intelligence to make trading decisions. Some platforms rely primarily on predefined rules, while others use AI to build strategies, interpret market conditions, or configure automated trading systems.

The best AI crypto trading bot depends on what you need: strategy automation, AI-assisted decision-making, beginner-friendly controls, or trading across multiple exchanges. This guide compares five platforms based on their available features, intended use cases, and practical limitations.

We looked at each platform’s automation features, strategy tools, backtesting options, supported exchanges, ease of use, pricing, and risk-management features. We also checked the information against each platform’s official website. Our picks are based on the features each bot offers and who it may suit best, rather than independently tested trading results. Keep in mind that features, fees, and exchange support can change over time.

3Commas is a crypto trading platform that combines automated bots with tools for managing and executing trades. It is widely used for multi-exchange order execution and parameter-driven  3Commas AI Trading Bot setups.

Its features include Dollar-Cost Averaging (DCA) bots, grid bots, signal-based trading, and SmartTrade order management.

The platform also offers an AI trading assistant that lets users describe a strategy in natural language. According to 3Commas, the assistant can configure a bot, run a backtest using historical market data, and prepare the strategy for launch.

Limitation: Bot capacity on the entry plan is small, and higher limits require Pro or Expert. Backtests also cannot fully reproduce future market conditions, slippage, liquidity constraints, or unexpected volatility.

3Commas is worth considering for traders who want to automate established trading strategies while retaining control over entry conditions, position sizing, and exits. It is particularly relevant to users who already understand concepts such as DCA, grid trading, and technical indicators.

Cryptohopper is a cloud-based engine that combines automated crypto trading with strategy-building, backtesting, and AI-assisted tools.

Its AI Strategy Designer helps traders choose strategies, signal providers, and TradingView alerts based on current market conditions. However, access depends on the subscription plan, so it’s worth checking the requirements before signing up.

Cryptohopper also has Cryptohopper.AI, a separate tool that lets users create trading bots and other trading tools simply by describing what they want in plain language. Although both use AI, they serve different purposes and shouldn’t be confused with each other.

Limitation: Access to certain AI features depends on the product and subscription tier. AI-generated strategies still require testing and monitoring before live deployment.

Cryptohopper trading bot suits traders who want to experiment with different strategies and automate their selection or execution. It is also relevant to users interested in building customized crypto trading tools without writing all the code themselves.

Pionex is a cryptocurrency exchange with AI trading bots built directly into its platform. Unlike third-party automation services that require users to connect exchange accounts, Pionex integrates bot functionality into the exchange itself.

Pionex offers 16 bots, including Grid Trading, Infinity Grid, Trailing Buy/Sell, Rebalancing, and Spot-Futures Arbitrage bots. The options also include PionexGPT, an AI-related feature that allows users to write custom trading strategies using natural language prompts.

Limitations:  Funds are held on the Pionex exchange rather than on an exchange you already use, so the AI trading bots cannot be applied to other exchanges.

Pionex is a good option for beginners who want to try automated trading without paying for a separate bot service or connecting to another exchange. It can also be useful for experienced traders who prefer to manage everything on one platform.

Coinrule focuses on rule-based crypto trading automation. Users can create strategies by setting simple rules rather than building a trading system entirely from scratch.

With features like Coinrule AI Cloud, users can also use plain language to create trading strategies, get help setting them up, test them against historical data, and connect with compatible AI assistants.

Limitation: Rule-based automation follows its configured conditions; it does not inherently understand market context or predict future prices. It doesn’t provide the level of mathematical detail and precise order book analysis that professional institutional traders need.

Coinrule is suitable for traders who know what conditions they want to trade but do not want to write the underlying code. It is also useful for users who want to test systematic strategies before connecting them to live trading.

Bitsgap is a crypto trading platform that brings everything together in one place, including automated crypto AI trading bots, portfolio management, analytics, and exchange connections. It offers different trading bots, such as Grid and DCA, to help users automate their strategies. Its AI Assistant also helps users configure their trading setups.

With support for multiple crypto exchanges, Bitsgap lets users manage their trading activities through a single interface.

Limitation: Futures bots are not available on the Basic plan.Exchange support and available features vary.

Bitsgap is a good option for traders who use multiple exchanges and want to manage their trading bots in one place. Its automation tools and analytics also make it easier to track strategies and monitor performance.

The best AI crypto trading bot is the one whose capabilities match your trading approach, not necessarily the one with the most AI features.

Before choosing a platform, compare these factors:

AI crypto trading bots can automate execution and reduce the need for constant manual monitoring, but profitability is never guaranteed. Results depend on strategy design, market conditions, execution costs, liquidity, and risk management.

Historical backtests are useful for evaluating a strategy, but they do not establish that it will perform similarly in live markets. Traders should test bots in simulation where possible, start with limited exposure, and monitor performance after deployment.

An AI label alone is not evidence of a trading advantage. Before selecting a bot, establish what the AI actually does, how trades are triggered, and how losses are managed.

The answer depends on the use case. Pionex requires no API setup or subscription, 3Commas builds bots from plain-English prompts, Bitsgap covers 17+ exchanges, and Cryptohopper offers a strategy marketplace.

No profitability can be assumed. Results depend on settings, fees, and market conditions, and losses are possible.

#5189. What is EIP-7702? The Ethereum Upgrade Behind the $6.4B Binance Hack

What is EIP-7702? The Ethereum Upgrade Behind the $6.4B Binance Hack

Ethereum has two kinds of accounts. Externally owned accounts (EOAs), the standard wallets most people use, are controlled by a private key and can do little more than send transactions. Smart contract accounts can run code, enabling features like spending limits, account recovery and paying fees in tokens other than ETH, but most users never moved to them.

EIP-7702 is an attempt to bridge that gap. Instead of asking users to migrate to new wallets, it lets existing EOAs borrow the code of a smart contract while keeping their address and funds.

This guide explains what EIP-7702 is, how it works, why developers wanted it, and how attackers used it in the largest crypto theft on record.

EIP-7702, titled "Set Code for EOAs," is an Ethereum Improvement Proposal written in May 2024 by Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin and developers Sam Wilson, Ansgar Dietrichs and lightclient, according to the official specification.

It was one of the headline changes in Pectra, a major Ethereum upgrade that went live on May 7, 2025.

"EIP-7702 lays the foundation we've needed for a long time," Ethereum core developer Preston Van Loon told Decrypt at the time. "While full abstraction won't be immediately available to end users with Pectra, this upgrade gives Ethereum the infrastructure to support it moving forward."

EIP-7702 is a change to Ethereum's core protocol, not a token or a separate blockchain, so there is nothing to buy.

EIP-7702 adds a new type of Ethereum transaction, the "set code transaction." It carries a list of authorizations, each signed with the private key of the account being upgraded, that names the address of a smart contract the account wants to use.

Once the transaction is processed, the account stores a small pointer, called a delegation indicator, to that contract. From then on, whenever anyone calls the account, Ethereum runs the contract's code as if it belonged to the account, with full access to its funds.

The delegation lasts until the account owner signs a new authorization, either pointing to a different contract or clearing the pointer to restore a plain EOA.

EIP-7702 marks delegated accounts using the byte 0xef, a code value that was banned in earlier upgrades so it could be reserved for special purposes like this.

The specification names three main features it was designed to deliver:

Those same features carry risks. Because delegated code gets "unrestricted access to the account," apps should never ask users to sign an EIP-7702 authorization, and wallets should not offer an interface for it, the specification warns. "There is no safe way to provide this interface," it says.

Scammers moved quickly. Within weeks of Pectra's launch, trading firm Wintermute found that more than 80% of EIP-7702 delegations pointed to copies of the same malicious "sweeper" contract, which automatically drains wallets whose keys have leaked, The Block reported in June 2025.

On October 29, 2026, an attacker moved some $6.4 billion out of Binance wallets on 10 blockchains, most of it within about 20 minutes. Blockchain analytics firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis both attributed the theft to TraderTraitor, the North Korean hacking group behind the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025.

On Ethereum, the attacker used an EIP-7702 delegation to turn a Binance hot wallet into a sweeper it controlled, with 50 authorizations signed in advance, according to TRM Labs. An operational wallet funded through crypto mixer Tornado Cash submitted the signed authorizations, which let the hot wallet run attacker-deployed code, and the attacker then called the wallet to sweep its assets into addresses it controlled, Chainalysis said.

Crucially, EIP-7702 delegations require a valid signature from the account being upgraded. Binance wallets on the other nine chains also sent funds to the attacker through ordinary signed transfers, which TRM said points to a compromise of Binance's hot wallet signing infrastructure rather than a flaw in Ethereum itself.

Binance has said its investigation began with a compromised engineer's laptop, and has since found "additional points of breach."

EIP-7702 is a first step toward full account abstraction, a long-standing goal of making every Ethereum account as flexible as a smart contract. Its authors designed it to be forward-compatible with that "endgame," so wallets built on it today should keep working as Ethereum's account model evolves.

The next step could come with Hegotá, the upgrade planned to follow Glamsterdam on Ethereum's roadmap. In February 2026, Buterin said that EIP-8141, which he called "an omnibus that wraps up and solves every remaining problem" account abstraction was meant to address, looked "possible to make happen within a year" in the Hegotá fork.

We have been talking about account abstraction ever since early 2016, see the original EIP-86: https://t.co/HYLSTLHgWH

Now, we finally have EIP-8141 ( https://t.co/jYqeS55j6P ), an omnibus that wraps up and solves every remaining problem that AA was…

— vitalik.eth (@VitalikButerin) February 28, 2026

"We have been talking about account abstraction ever since early 2016," Buterin wrote, adding that developers are also discussing whether existing accounts could join the new framework, which would give them batching and sponsored transactions natively.

It is part of a wider rebuild. In July 2026, Buterin described a new draft of Ethereum's long-term roadmap as the network's biggest overhaul since the Merge, its 2022 switch to proof of stake.

The end of October 2026 was marked by the largest incident in the history of the crypto market — the $6.3 billion hack of the Binance exchange. This case exposed the vulnerability of the instant exchange (swaps) infrastructure.

While the automated systems of the North Korean group TraderTraitor withdrew $242 million via the Tron blockchain in the first two days, decentralized bridges and liquidity aggregators de facto became the main tool for legalizing the stolen funds.

Against this backdrop, the head of NEAR Intents Alex Shevchenko issued a warning to cryptocurrency wallet developers. His position is pragmatic: focusing exclusively on finding the best rate for the user turns services into unwitting accomplices in cybercrimes.

Since around $3.5 billion still remains under the hackers’ control after a wave of emergency freezes, regulatory pressure on the Web3 sector will inevitably increase. To minimize risks, the head of NEAR Intents formulated three basic survival rules for modern crypto wallets when choosing integration partners:

For wallet developers, the problem is structural. A single swap often passes through several protocols at once — an aggregator, a bridge and multiple liquidity pools — and each hop dilutes responsibility.

If any link in this chain processes tainted funds, the wallet through which the transaction was initiated shares the reputational damage and, increasingly, the legal exposure.

This is why due diligence on integration partners is shifting from an optional step to a core product requirement.

Investments in compliance and integration security are no longer a boring formality. The market has reached a point where the reputational and legal cleanliness of a service is valued far higher than saving a few cents on fees.

Water.org has used Ripple Payments to move more than $3.2 million across four markets.

Settlement times in Mexico and Brazil dropped from two to three days to same-day, while payment processing became available around the clock instead of being limited by a single daily banking cutoff.

Transaction fees fell by as much as 66 percent, so a larger share of every dollar reaches borrowers rather than intermediaries.

Ripple committed $6 million over three years to support Water.org programs such as WaterCredit, which partners with local financial institutions to offer affordable loans for household taps, toilets, and piped connections.

Finance as a tool to solve the water crisis 💧@Water co-founders Matt Damon and Gary White joined @bgarlinghouse on the Swell main stage to share how Ripple Payments and RLUSD are helping @Water reach more people, faster. pic.twitter.com/VXdttesBK6

Separately, Water.org received a $1.25 million grant in Ripple’s RLUSD through the Stablecoin Impact Fund. That capital is intended to expand stablecoin-enabled WaterCredit disbursements into Indonesia, the Philippines, and Uganda.

Water.org will also begin using Ripple’s Wallet-as-a-Service technology to manage digital assets as the programs scale. Beyond the direct funding, Ripple joined Get Blue, the Water.org movement modeled after the (RED) campaign, as its exclusive digital-asset and fintech partner.

Founding brand partners include Gap, Amazon, Starbucks, and Ecolab. Ripple’s first year of Get Blue support helped reach 400,000 people, with the three-year commitment expected to support 1.2 million as Water.org works toward its broader goal of reaching 200 million people by 2030.

Gary White, co-founder and CEO of Water.org, said the actual water crisis is fundamentally a funding-flow problem rather than a lack of capital, and that Ripple’s infrastructure has shown what efficient movement of money looks like in practice.

Brad Garlinghouse, Ripple’s CEO, noted that the partnership demonstrates the original promise of crypto and blockchain: making money move faster, more efficiently, and globally for real-world needs.

💧🌍 WATER IS LIFE. CRYPTO IS CHANGING THE GAME! 🚀Hollywood superstar Matt Damon in conversation with @bgarlinghouse is helping tackle the global water crisis through https://t.co/AMHUwOVte1, and Ripple is part of a bigger conversation about using financial innovation to… pic.twitter.com/U42l8YvnZM

White and Matt Damon joined Garlinghouse for a fireside chat at Ripple Swell in New York.

The expanded setup combines traditional philanthropic capital with on-chain settlement and custody so that repaid loans can be recycled into new lending through vehicles such as the WaterEquity Everspring Fund.

For Water.org, the practical result is more of each donated or invested dollar reaching families that need household water connections. For Ripple, it is another demonstration of its payments and stablecoin stack operating outside pure trading venues and inside humanitarian finance.

#5185. Lisk Officially Shuts Down Blockchain After 10 Years

Long-standing blockchain project Lisk has officially ended its blockchain operations after 10 years of existence, moving on to a new financial platform for businesses.

Lisk announced on Nov. 2 the official shutdown of its blockchain after 10 years of existence. This marks the end of one of the longest-lived blockchains in the crypto world.

"Today, the Lisk Chain has officially shut down," the project said in an X post.

With the blockchain shutdown, Lisk has ended its Portal and Bridge services. The rest of the blockchain's infrastructure is also being powered down.

The blockchain shutdown marks a significant milestone in the evolution of the Lisk project, which was launched in 2016 and has seen several changes over the years.

The Lisk team, however, has noted that the shutdown of the blockchain does not spell the end of the Lisk project.

The company is transforming into a new financial platform, one that enables businesses to manage both traditional currencies and stablecoins in one place.

"For 10 years, Lisk built onchain with developers, stakers and holders that made Lisk what it is," Lisk said.

The Lisk project has made it clear that its native token, LSK, will continue to exist even as the blockchain closes shop.

According to the team, LSK will still exist on Ethereum as the loyalty token for its new business financial platform.

In addition, the project announced plans to burn approximately 5.23 million LSK tokens left in its staking rewards pool.

The total figure includes unallocated rewards to users as well as unclaimed earned rewards.

The LSK tokens are set to be burned, permanently removing them from circulation. This will also lower the overall supply of the cryptocurrency.

This comes after a large burn of LSK tokens in September. At the time, Lisk burned 100 million LSK tokens after making the decision to wind down its decentralized autonomous organization (DAO) through a governance vote.

The burn event reduced the LSK token's supply from 400 million to 300 million LSK.

Lisk intends to introduce new use cases for LSK in 2027. This will allow businesses to earn rewards in the token and use LSK for platform fees.

#5184. What Happens To Your Body When You Cut Back—But Don’t Quit—Alcohol?

If you’ve spent any time on social media recently, your feed is probably packed with people talking up how amazing they feel without alcohol in their lives. But while a growing body of research has found that no amount of alcohol is technically good for you, it’s understandable to still want to enjoy the odd glass of wine or cocktail with friends.

There are a few studies out there on the potential health impacts of avoiding alcohol, but what happens if you just cut back? An all-or-nothing approach doesn’t work for some people, so it’s fair to wonder if you’d still be getting health perks by going this route.

We tapped two doctors who study the impact of alcohol on the body to learn more.

Meet the experts: Megan Strowger, PhD, a post-doctoral research associate at University at Buffalo; Emily A. Gordon, MD, MPH, assistant professor of medicine and program director of Addiction Medicine Fellowship at Rutgers New Jersey Medical School

You’ll still get plenty of health perks if you just have the odd drink, says Megan Strowger, PhD, a post-doctoral research associate at University at Buffalo who recently studied the impact on the body of cutting out alcohol for a month. In fact, she says cutting back can have a “profound impact” on your health, especially if you’ve been a heavy drinker in the past.

Strowger points to an older clinical trial that found people had lower blood pressure, better liver function, and reported a better quality of life within four months of cutting back on their drinking. That shows that “even a moderate reduction in consumption can lead to meaningful improvements for both the body and mind,” Strowger says.

It’s not a bad idea to leave room for a little alcohol in your life if you enjoy it and don’t struggle with alcohol use disorder, says Emily A. Gordon, MD, MPH, assistant professor of medicine and program director of Addiction Medicine Fellowship at Rutgers New Jersey Medical School. “There is a benefit to having a glass of wine to relax and enjoy time with friends, as long as it’s not chronic use,” she says. “The mental health benefits need to be weighed along with the physical.”

There is no hard and fast number, but there is some general guidance to consider. “The World Health Organization categorizes drinking into different ‘risk levels,’ and research shows that moving down just one or two of these levels can lead to significant physical health improvements and fewer alcohol-related complications a year later,” Strowger says.

Gordon points out that there are healthy drinking limits in place (no more than two drinks a day for men and one drink a day for women). “But they are probably higher than they should be,” she says. “As long as you’re moderating your intake, it’s likely healthy.”

If you really want to focus on health, Gordon suggests just trying to minimize how much you drink. “Ultimately, the healthiest approach is to keep consumption as low as possible, as there is no level of use that is considered entirely risk-free,” she says.

You may be just fine deciding you’re only going to drink here and there, but some people prefer a little more guidance. If you fall into the second camp, Gordon recommends thinking about when you tend to drink. “Is it to ease a little anxiety, socially, or out of boredom?” she says. “Then, try to think of healthier things that can be substituted.” That might mean incorporating daily stress-reducing walks into your day, taking up a new hobby, or diving into all the NA options out there to find something you enjoy that you can sip while you socialize with friends.

Tracking how often you drink (including the type and number of drinks you have) can be helpful, too, Strowger says. “This habit is associated with sustained reductions in drinking even a month later,” she says.

If you respond well to clear boundaries, Strowger recommends giving yourself a specific limit on drinks you’ll have in each sitting or per week. “However, it is important to practice self-compassion,” she says. “If you don't always hit your targets, simply carry on and try again during the next week or occasion.” It can even be helpful to practice ways to politely decline when someone offers you a drink after you’ve hit your personal limit, she says.

Ultimately, just do your best. “In general, the less you drink, the better,” Gordon says. “But we do need to recognize the importance of socializing and spending time with friends.” Basically, don’t feel bad about catching up with your crew over a glass of wine. It’s unlikely to hurt your health—and could even give your mental health a boost.

#5183. Elon Musk, CZ Trade Blows Over SpaceX Shares After $6.4B Binance Hack

Elon Musk, CZ Trade Blows Over SpaceX Shares After $6.4B Binance Hack

Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao, better known as CZ, called out Elon Musk on Friday after the billionaire appeared to mock the exchange following a $6.4 billion hack—the largest in history—reminding him that Binance holds SpaceX shares worth more than $1 billion.

"Elon, have a lot of respect for you, but bad time to troll. Please stop," CZ wrote on X. "Our SPCX shares (from our $500m investment in your Twitter takeover) are worth more than a billion. Would appreciate if you show a little support. Thanks!"

The exchange followed Musk's response to a post estimating that, as a lot of the stolen funds have been frozen, Binance's losses could reach around $1 billion, despite holding approximately $144 billion in assets under custody.

Musk had replied to the discussion with a grimacing emoji, prompting another user to share an old post from former FTX CEO Sam Bankman-Fried claiming his exchange had enough money to cover its losses. FTX famously collapsed weeks later.

Elon, have a lot of respect for you, but bad time to troll. Please stop.

Our SPCX shares (from our $500m investment in your Twitter takeover) are worth more than a billion.

Would appreciate if you show a little support. Thanks!

— CZ 🔶 BNB (@cz_binance) October 30, 2026

CZ had initially responded to the loss estimate by saying the damage might be somewhat higher but that Binance would still be able to cover it. Musk's emoji appeared to draw an uncomfortable parallel with the FTX episode, although he did not elaborate on what he meant.

Of course, CZ didn't imply anything else about what Binance may do with its SpaceX shares.

Binance co-CEO Yi He also joined the exchange, addressing CZ in a post that appeared to respond to the suggestion that the company might need to liquidate its SpaceX holdings.

"Reporting to the major shareholder: Our company's revenue for the year is sufficient to cover the losses, so we do not yet need to sell the SpaceX shares you are bullish on," she wrote, adding a shrugging emoji.

CZ subsequently clarified that he had never suggested selling the shares. He said he was simply showing Musk some of the funds Binance had available, hoping to reassure him about the exchange's financial position.

😂 did say anything about selling SPCX shares, was just saying/showing some funds that he might know, so that he can be less worried.

— CZ 🔶 BNB (@cz_binance) October 30, 2026

The argument comes as Binance deals with the largest cryptocurrency theft on record. At least $6.4 billion in crypto was taken from wallets associated with the exchange on Thursday, October 29, across multiple blockchains.

Just yesterday, initial reports showed that at least $5.57 billion had left Binance-linked wallets across Ethereum, Bitcoin, and Tron. The attackers moved funds through several transactions, including a transfer of more than $1.6 billion in USDT to a newly created Ethereum address.

The incident also exposed an important weakness in how cryptocurrency can be recovered after a theft. Tether and Circle, the companies behind the USDT and USDC stablecoins, froze approximately $1.8 billion in assets associated with the attackers in the initial response, then subsequently froze a total of $2.39 billion. Unlike those tokens, Ethereum cannot be frozen by a central issuer, making it harder to stop stolen funds once they are converted.

The attackers subsequently used decentralized exchanges such as Uniswap and lending protocol Aave to move funds into Ethereum. These platforms allow users to trade or borrow cryptocurrency without relying on a traditional intermediary to approve each transaction. Decrypt tracked wallets receiving tens of thousands of ETH through these operations, including 19,762 ETH borrowed against approximately $60 million in USDT.

The suspected attackers have also been linked to North Korea. In a Friday report, blockchain analytics firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking group previously blamed for the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025. Chainalysis estimated the Binance theft at approximately $6.4 billion.

Binance has since said it has reserved more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover the incident, including $5 billion already held in the same tokens that were stolen. The exchange said it is acquiring the remaining assets through market and over-the-counter purchases, which can take longer when certain tokens have limited liquidity.

#5181. Trezor lifts password ceiling after Coldcard’s $100M wallet thefts

Trezor cited July’s Coldcard attacks, in which strong passphrases helped protect some users whose wallet recovery information was compromised.

Hardware wallet maker Trezor has increased the maximum length of optional wallet passphrases from 50 to 128 characters.

On Sunday, Trezor said the change is available in its Trezor Suite with updated device firmware. Older firmware still limits passphrases to 50 characters.

According to Trezor, a passphrase acts like an additional password that users set alongside their wallet’s recovery phrase. An attacker who obtains the recovery phrase would still need the correct passphrase to access funds in that wallet.

Trezor cited the Coldcard attacks in July, when a firmware flaw caused some devices to generate recovery phrases with insufficient randomness, allowing attackers to reconstruct them. Trezor said strong, unique passphrases protected some affected users.

The update follows a separate warning involving Trezor’s own devices.

On Friday, the company advised customers who bought wallets from former authorized reseller CryptoBilis since March to move their funds to new wallets.

An Indonesian customer reported a suspected implant inside a Trezor Safe 5 that could capture on-screen information, including recovery phrases, and transmit it over a cellular network. Trezor said Friday it had not examined the device and had received no reports of related losses.

#5180. XRP’s Security Fix Puts Validator Trust Under Scrutiny

Home » Trendsetter News » XRP’s Security Fix Puts Validator Trust Under Scrutiny

An XRP Ledger security patch released before full code disclosure has sparked debate over vulnerability management and validator influence.

A security patch released before its full code was made public is at the center of a dispute over XRP Ledger governance. In a video addressing the controversy, Kamilah Stevenson, a finance commentator and longtime XRP holder, argues that the restricted disclosure protected the network rather than substantiated allegations of fraud.

The criticism came from Cyber Capital fund manager Justin Bonds, who, according to Stevenson, challenged both the upgrade process and the influence of recommended validator lists. The dispute raises two distinct questions for investors: how developers handle dangerous vulnerabilities, and how much discretion network operators retain.

Stevenson says a researcher reported an overflow vulnerability through the XRP Ledger’s bug bounty program on September 22. The flaw, which she says had existed since around 2015, potentially allowed an attacker to obtain XRP improperly or create unauthorized tokens.

According to her account, developers released version 3.4.1 on September 25 without immediately publishing the full fix code. More than 80% of main validators upgraded that day, and an amendment activated on October 9, leaving nodes without the update unable to remain synchronized.

Dr. Stevenson reports that a subsequent ledger audit found no exploitation or unauthorized XRP creation. The transcript does not identify the auditor or provide the underlying report.

She compares the response with Bitcoin Core’s handling of a 2018 vulnerability: developers initially disclosed a crash risk, withholding its inflation implications until users had time to upgrade.

“You protect the network first and you explain second,” she says. That comparison supports delayed vulnerability disclosure, though it does not by itself resolve concerns about inspecting the XRP update.

Stevenson acknowledges that publishers of recommended Unique Node Lists wield influence because many operators adopt those defaults. Operators can choose their own lists, she says, while Ripple runs only one validator on the most commonly used list.

She also points to the amendment threshold: more than 80% validator support sustained for two weeks. Those safeguards challenge the idea that Ripple can unilaterally rewrite ledger rules, but validator ownership alone does not settle questions about influence over defaults.

In a nutshell, the promised code release and technical write-up would offer firmer grounds for judging this episode than either a fraud allegation or assurances from an XRP holder.

#5179. Binance Restores Withdrawals for Ripple's RLUSD Stablecoin

Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has fully enabled withdrawals for Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin on the Ethereum network. This move is part of the exchange's gradual service recovery process after the massive $6.3 billion hack.

On Nov. 3, the exchange released an update on the next stage of its withdrawal restoration plan, with a new list of cryptocurrencies available for withdrawal.

Interestingly, the new list of assets includes Ripple’s US dollar-backed stablecoin RLUSD and a number of other stablecoins.

This announcement follows Binance’s gradual restoration of withdrawals, which began on Nov. 1 after a brief halt due to one of the largest hacks in the crypto industry.

As per the latest recovery update from Binance, the exchange began its second significant withdrawal restoration phase at 04:00 UTC on Nov. 3.

Apart from RLUSD, the cryptocurrency exchange is now gradually re-enabling withdrawals for dozens of cryptocurrencies on multiple blockchain networks, including Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, Solana, XRP Ledger, Sui, Arbitrum, Optimism, Tron and Base.

For Ethereum, the list of cryptocurrencies now available for withdrawal includes Shiba Inu (SHIB), Chainlink (LINK), Worldcoin (WLD), Ondo (ONDO) and Ethena (ENA).

At the same time, the cryptocurrency exchange has also added XRP and a number of other top crypto assets to its list of withdrawals that will soon be re-enabled on BNB Smart Chain.

The crypto exchange emphasized that not all of the listed assets will be enabled for withdrawal at once. Instead, each asset and network combination will be re-enabled individually after the necessary security and operational checks are completed.

“We will gradually re-enable more assets & networks in stages once we complete the relevant security checks,” Binance said.

At the same time, the crypto exchange also warned that there may be delays due to traffic during this restoration process. Meanwhile, cryptocurrency deposits remain functional.

Initially, Binance started re-enabling withdrawals on Nov. 1 for top cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), XRP, Solana (SOL), Dogecoin (DOGE) and Zcash (ZEC), as well as major stablecoins USDT and USDC.

The latest withdrawal restoration update comes only a few days after the cryptocurrency exchange suffered a massive hack on Oct. 29, which resulted in the theft of about $6.3 billion in crypto.

The FBI officially identified the perpetrators of the hack as North Korean hackers linked to the infamous TraderTraitor operation on Oct. 31.

The U.S. agency revealed that hackers have been converting stolen cryptocurrencies mostly into Ethereum as a potential path toward laundering the assets through decentralized finance platforms and crypto swap services.

More withdrawal restorations will follow as Binance moves forward with its security checks and recovery processes.

#5176. Binance Sets Aside $6.34B to Cover Hack Losses, CEO Says 'Your Assets Are Safe'

Binance Sets Aside $6.34B to Cover Hack Losses, CEO Says 'Your Assets Are Safe'

Binance will cover every dollar lost in this week's hack with its own money, CEO Richard Teng said in a video address on Friday, adding that customer funds were never touched.

"We are committed to covering all hacked losses through our company funds. Your assets are safe," Teng said, according to a transcript he tweeted.

An update on the security incident. pic.twitter.com/qn2804fO5z

— Richard Teng (@_RichardTeng) October 30, 2026

Binance has reserved more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover the stolen assets, $5 billion of which is already held in the exact tokens taken, including USDC, USDT, BTC, ETH and BNB, he said. The exchange is buying the rest through market and over-the-counter channels.

Teng said the hack hit Binance's own hot wallet, not customer funds. "We never use any customer funds, so they are not impacted," he said, adding that most user assets are held in cold wallets and only moved into a hot wallet when a user withdraws. Binance's ability to absorb a loss of this size comes from keeping much of its operating earnings in crypto, he said.

Binance had earlier said it would cover all losses from its SAFU emergency fund and company funds.

Teng said the hack "was not carried out by one person." Binance initially traced it to a compromised laptop but has since found additional points of breach. The attacker also used a self-destruct mechanism that destroyed tooling and traces along the way, making the attack harder to investigate, Teng said.

The attacker used EIP-7702, an Ethereum feature that lets standard wallets run smart contract code, to obtain onchain execution approval over a hot wallet, according to Teng. "That delegation did not pass through our normal approval controls," he said, which is why Binance paused withdrawals to rebuild and retest its infrastructure. Blockchain analytics firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis have attributed the theft to North Korean hacking group TraderTraitor.

Binance hopes to restore withdrawals before its Sunday deadline, Teng said, and is carrying out a full security review covering endpoints, cloud, key management and signing. It plans to publish a full proof of reserves report by Monday, with an initial view before then.

The attacker is still moving funds. Between 11:37 a.m. and 12:12 p.m. ET on Friday, a Tron wallet that Arkham attributes to the hacker sent about 5.19 million TRX, worth roughly $1.73 million, to 12 addresses, according to Arkham data.

All markets are now unfrozen across Aave V3 and V4.

They were frozen as a precaution after initial reports, which paused new deposits and borrows while withdrawals and repayments continued as normal.

Decentralized lending protocol Aave, where the attacker borrowed ETH against USDT while racing stablecoin freezes, according to TRM Labs, said on Friday that it had unfrozen all markets on its V3 and V4 deployments. It had frozen them as a precaution after the first reports of the hack, pausing new deposits and borrowing while withdrawals and repayments continued. "Aave was unaffected, and all positions remain overcollateralized," founder Stani Kulechov wrote.

Binance co-founder Changpeng "CZ" Zhao said that while the $6.3 billion theft is the largest in dollar terms, it is not the largest in Bitcoin terms, pointing to Mt. Gox's loss of 650,000 BTC, more than 5% of the supply. Unlike at Mt. Gox and FTX, where nearly all users were affected, Binance is covering the losses itself, he said. "It hurts, but we survive," Zhao wrote.
