#5174. Evernorth’s Warrants Could Raise $135 Million.. Or Not

Home » Trendsetter News » Evernorth’s Warrants Could Raise $135 Million.. Or Not

With millions of shares becoming tradable, financing terms & decisions will shape the company’s ability to expand holdings.

Evernorth could receive roughly $135 million from outstanding warrants, or nothing, depending on how they are exercised. In a new crypto research, a popular analyst examining the XRP treasury company’s financing argues that this distinction matters more than its stock’s reported one-day collapse of roughly 50%.

The company holds about 473 million XRP, according to Fire Hustle. Its ability to expand that position depends partly on its share price, financing terms and whether investors decide to sell newly tradable stock.

Fire Hustle identifies approximately 11.7 million warrants, each carrying an $11.50 exercise price. Full exercise for cash would bring Evernorth roughly $135 million, potentially funding additional XRP purchases.

A sustained share price of at least $18 – on 20 trading days within a 30-trading-day period – would allow the company to call the warrants, subject to the terms described in the video. Holders would then face a deadline to exercise before the warrants were redeemed for a nominal amount.

But management could require cashless exercise instead. That would produce fewer new shares while bringing in no exercise proceeds. “The option that Evernorth picks,” Fire Hustle says, determines whether this financing route delivers fresh purchasing power for XRP.

The distinction is important: a rising stock price alone would not guarantee another large XRP purchase.

According to the YouTube video, cash investors including SBI Holdings could sell more than 13 million shares once the relevant resale registration becomes effective.

Fire Hustle says those investors did not sign the six-month lockups covering Ripple, a Larsen family trust and Arrington’s fund.

That potential supply is substantial beside the fewer than five million shares the analyst says remained publicly held after heavy redemptions by the blank-check company’s investors.

Still, eligibility to sell is not evidence of an imminent exit. The analyst estimates SBI paid in the mid-to-high teens per share and notes its longstanding relationship with Ripple, suggesting less incentive to sell near its entry price.

A premium to those assets can support further purchases; a discount can undermine that strategy and make buybacks more attractive.

Fire Hustle raises XRP sales as a possible consequence, not an announced company plan. Investors therefore have two distinct developments to watch: when restricted shares become tradable, and whether warrant exercises actually put cash into Evernorth.

#5172. Vitalik is making private Ethereum payments without a crypto website

Retaining local code can reduce repeated website delivery while leaving package updates, signatures and submission as separate trust decisions.

His objection goes beyond screen clutter. A website can deliver application code again whenever someone returns, leaving the user dependent on what the server supplies each time. Keeping a local application can reduce that repeated delivery exposure. It also moves a consequential decision onto the user: which software revision to install, retain and eventually replace.

The wallet he linked makes the trade-off concrete. Its documentation warns that the CLI is unaudited, under active development and written with AI assistance. It tells users to avoid mainnet unless they understand what they are doing and the possibility of catastrophic fund loss.

Control over a downloaded interface matters because the accepted code sits between a payment instruction and the signature authorizing it. Choosing when that code changes can reduce one recurring exposure, while its dependencies and signing access determine what the installed software can do.

The practical gain is the ability to keep a chosen application revision rather than obtaining the website interface again on each visit. Accepting a replacement revision creates another delivery decision. For this source-build route, that decision also involves the dependency set and the tools that turn source into executable software. A familiar project name alone does not describe all the code being accepted.

The documented installation route also shows what “local” entails. The project's instructions call for installing dependencies with npm install, building the application with npm run build, and running a local launcher. At commit 0ef5c44, the documentation, manifest, lockfile and implementation describe the same application revision. Its manifest identifies version 0.1.0 and requires Node.js 22 or later. Buterin's account does not identify his installed revision.

The manifest fixes direct dependency versions, including viem and several Kohaku packages. It also pins a separate kohaku-artifacts Git dependency to a commit. The corresponding lockfile records resolved registry packages and integrity hashes. The application therefore has a software supply chain even when its interface runs on the user's machine.

Kohaku-cli's public-transfer and Railgun unshield paths show why a pause before submission can mean different things. An ordinary public-transfer dry run returns without sending the transaction; a prepared Railgun unshield can already contain a signature.

For an ordinary, non-batched public transfer, the transfer implementation simulates the transaction and returns dry-run output without submission. The broadcast path requires the sender's private key, constructs a local wallet client and sends the transaction. The wallet-client code derives its signing account from that private key.

Private operations expose an additional wrinkle. The unshield command can output a prepared Railgun UserOperation that is already signed, even when broadcasting is withheld. A UserOperation is an account-operation payload that compatible tooling can submit. The separate broadcast implementation expects a signed operation and then sends it through a Pimlico bundler.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

For that path, withholding submission can still leave a signed operation ready for compatible tooling to submit later. Calling the result “prepared” therefore does not make it universally unsigned. Software that may construct an authorization, software that may sign it and software that may submit it need to be assessed as distinct sources of authority, even when one CLI coordinates them.

Human confirmation is another separate choice. In the inspected public-transfer path, a suitably configured caller with wallet access can use --non-interactive together with --broadcast to submit without a further confirmation prompt. Wallet unlocking, required parameters, chain matching and simulation checks still apply. The capability is relevant to scripts and agents; it does not reveal whether Buterin uses unattended payments.

The README describes an encrypted seed on disk and owner-restricted password files for POSIX automation. Those measures govern stored secrets and how a process obtains access to them. They do not, by themselves, establish an independent spending limit or recipient policy once the process can use the signer.

CryptoSlate has previously covered the wallet-permission problem for local AI. Delivery control adds another dimension: a user can retain a chosen interface revision, while that code operates within whatever signing and submission authority it receives.

Software provenance offers a way to examine the delivery side more rigorously. It records where an artifact came from and how it was built. The SLSA verification standard describes checking a provenance signature, matching the artifact's digest, recognizing a trusted builder and comparing the stated source and build parameters with expected values.

These checks can help distinguish an expected build from a substituted artifact or an unintended build source. They still depend on which builders and source expectations the verifier trusts.

Dependency checking remains its own task. SLSA describes recursive verification of resolved dependencies as an optional additional step. Authenticating the top-level artifact does not automatically authenticate every input to it.

Correct origin and build history can accompany application logic that the user would still reject.

Buterin's experiment points to a concrete form of user control: choosing the application code that stays on the machine and deciding when to accept replacement code. Its value depends on carrying that control through dependency selection and the signer.

#5171. From Uptober to Hacktober: Are Bitcoin’s seasonal patterns becoming obsolete?

Bitcoin lost 7.3% in October 2026 after another decline the previous year, despite the month’s historically strong returns, as analysts reassess seasonal signals.

Bitcoin’s back-to-back October losses have put its “Uptober” reputation under the microscope as analysts weigh seasonal trends against institutional demand and economic conditions.

Bitcoin fell 7.3% in October 2026, following a roughly 4% decline a year earlier, according to CoinGlass data.

The losses defied October’s historically bullish reputation, which earned it the nickname “Uptober.” This year, industry figures turned to darker labels, including “Black October” and “Hacktober,” amid a wave of crypto security incidents, including Binance’s record-breaking $6.3 billion hack.

October has historically delivered Bitcoin’s highest median return at 15.4%, with gains in 10 of 13 years through 2025, according to Andrew Yang, a researcher at crypto analytics firm Kaiko.

September’s historically bearish reputation has weakened as well. Bitcoin has posted gains every September since 2023, which could reflect traders buying ahead of an expected October rally, Yang told Cointelegraph.

Median monthly Bitcoin return by calendar month since January 2013. Source: Kaiko

Bitcoin’s narrowing price swings may also be making seasonal trends less pronounced, Yang said. Its typical monthly move has declined from 14% between 2013 and 2016 to 9.6% since 2024, leaving less room for sharp seasonal rallies, he added.

Analysts also pointed to institutional investment and broader economic conditions as increasingly important influences on Bitcoin’s price.

Justin d’Anethan, head of research at Arctic Digital, pointed to exchange-traded fund (ETF) flows and corporate Bitcoin buyers, saying their investment decisions are shaped more by liquidity, interest rates and investment mandates than seasonal trading narratives.

Related: Bitcoin ETF flows give mixed read on institutional demand: CoinShares

US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $515 million in net outflows in October, while spot Ether ETFs saw a record $1.61 billion in monthly withdrawals.

Yang cautioned that spot Bitcoin ETFs, approved in January 2024, are too recent to assess. Still, Bitcoin “increasingly trades like a macro asset, driven more by economic data and institutional flows than by the calendar,” he said.

Despite two consecutive October losses, analysts cautioned against writing off Uptober entirely.

Julio Moreno, head of research at CryptoQuant, said October has generally performed better during Bitcoin bull markets and worse during bear markets, making the broader market cycle an important factor when comparing returns.

“Price performance depends more on spot demand dynamics than cyclical patterns, and demand doesn’t care about the calendar,” Moreno told Cointelegraph.

Related: Bitcoin risks worst October in 12 years as tech sell-off spreads to gold

Markus Levin, co-founder of XYO, said that traders may be anticipating seasonal gains earlier. “When enough people expect a rally in October, the rally gets priced in before the month arrives,” he said.

“Uptober has historical validity but, like other seasonality metrics, it can also fail at times,” said Arctic Digital’s d’Anethan.

Magazine: Cybersecurity’s Black October: How to protect yourself

#5170. Secret Service, FBI Join Binance Hack Probe as Circle Freezes $823 Million

Secret Service, FBI Join Binance Hack Probe as Circle Freezes $823 Million

Binance is working with the FBI and U.S. Secret Service after hackers stole $6.4 billion from the cryptocurrency exchange, as Circle joins the recovery effort by freezing more than $800 million in assets connected to the attack, according to Reuters.

A person familiar with the matter told Reuters that Binance was cooperating with law enforcement agencies around the world, including both U.S. agencies. The FBI confirmed it was aware of the incident and was working with public and private partners to assess its scope and coordinate investigative steps. The Secret Service remained silent.

Investigating financial crimes is part of the Secret Service’s job, beyond its better-known responsibility of protecting the president. The agency also investigates computer crimes, unauthorized access to computer systems, and crimes involving digital currencies.

Circle, the company behind USDC, a stablecoin designed to maintain a value of $1, has separately confirmed that it is coordinating with law enforcement. CEO Jeremy Allaire said the company had frozen more than $800 million in USDC associated with the Binance incident and would continue supporting the investigation.

Tether, which issues the competing USDT stablecoin, froze another $1.5 billion in tokens. Both companies can blacklist specific blockchain addresses, preventing the tokens they issue from being transferred out of those wallets. That ability gives stablecoin companies an unusual role in crypto investigations: they can effectively immobilize stolen money before investigators identify the people responsible.

Tether froze more than 1.567B USDT related to a potential Binance exchange hack.

Protecting the industry and our partners is our main priority.

— Paolo Ardoino 🤖 (@paoloardoino) October 29, 2026

This is not the first time the Secret Service has worked alongside crypto companies to investigate digital asset crimes. In April, Operation Atlantic—a joint effort involving the Secret Service, the U.K.'s National Crime Agency, Binance, Coinbase, and other crypto firms— identified more than 20,000 victims of approval phishing scams, traced $45 million in stolen funds and froze $12 million.

The Binance investigation also comes against the backdrop of a growing number of attacks attributed to North Korea. Blockchain intelligence firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis have both linked the $6.3 billion theft to TraderTraitor, a hacking group associated with the country's cyber operations. The same group has been linked to the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025, which the FBI also attributed to North Korean hackers.

North Korean attackers have targeted Binance itself before, including through attempts to infiltrate the exchange by posing as job applicants. In an interview with Decrypt in 2025, Binance Chief Security Officer Jimmy Su said North Korean operatives were contacting employees on LinkedIn every day, sometimes using fake interviews to deliver malware to their devices.

Binance has said it will cover all losses using company funds and its Secure Asset Fund for Users, an emergency reserve designed to protect customers in the event of a security breach. CEO Richard Teng said on Friday that the company had reserved more than $6.34 billion to cover the stolen assets, while approximately $3 billion had already been located or frozen with the help of industry partners.

The exchange initially suspected that a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer had provided the attackers with access to its systems. It has since identified additional points of breach and said it found no evidence that wallet private keys had been leaked. Withdrawals remain suspended while Binance reviews its security infrastructure, with the company targeting a resumption by Sunday.

Strategy‘s deployable USD Cash fell 45.3% during the week ended Nov. 1, from $242 million to $133 million, as preferred-stock buybacks exceeded its Bitcoin purchases.

That balance is available for broader treasury uses. Strategy also held a separate $4.79 billion USD Reserve intended for preferred-stock dividends and debt interest.

The purchase increased Strategy's holdings to 849,327 BTC, acquired for an aggregate $64 billion at an average price of $75,451 per coin.

The acquisition marked a return to larger Bitcoin purchases after Michael Saylor's firm suspended buying for a week while concentrating its spending on preferred-stock repurchases.

Strategy had acquired just 334 BTC, 250 BTC and 267 BTC in the first three reporting weeks of October, respectively. Its latest purchase was the largest since Sept. 28, when the company disclosed acquiring 1,665 BTC for approximately $143 million.

Strategy sold approximately 1,178,552 shares of its MSTR common stock through its at-the-market offering program, generating $164 million in net proceeds.

However, only $66 million, or about 40%, went toward purchasing Bitcoin. The remaining $99 million was allocated to the company's deployable USD Cash balance, which has come under pressure from its increasingly aggressive preferred-stock repurchase program.

#5167. $8 Million Crypto Kidnapping Lands Texas Brothers 15-Year Prison Terms

$8 Million Crypto Kidnapping Lands Texas Brothers 15-Year Prison Terms

Two Texas brothers have been sentenced to a combined 326 months in prison for a violent home-invasion robbery in which they held a Minnesota family at gunpoint for hours and forced the father to hand over more than $8 million in cryptocurrency.

Raymond Christian Garcia and Isiah Angelo Garcia, both of Waller, Texas, were sentenced on Thursday to 180 months and 186 months respectively, or 15 and 15-and-a-half years, by U.S. District Judge Donovan Frank in St. Paul, according to the Justice Department. Both had pleaded guilty in June.

According to court documents, the brothers traveled from Texas to Grant, Minnesota, and on Sept. 19, 2025, broke into the victim’s home, zip-tied the family and held them at gunpoint for more than nine hours while demanding access to the father’s crypto accounts.

When he failed to transfer the amount they expected, they forced him to drive one of the brothers to the family’s cabin in upstate Minnesota to retrieve additional hardware wallets and move the funds. In total, they compelled him to transfer over $8 million. The pair fled after the victim’s son called 911, and were later arrested near Houston.

“The Garcia brothers committed a brazen and calculated act of violence against the victim and his family,” U.S. Attorney Daniel Rosen said in a statement. The FBI’s Christopher Dotson said the brothers “violated the sanctity of a home” in “a brazen act of violence and greed.”

The case is a stark example of a “wrench attack,” in which criminals use physical force rather than hacking to seize crypto.

Such attacks have surged alongside crypto’s rising prices: Chainalysis counted 46 violent incidents in the first half of 2026 with more than $30 million stolen, while CertiK pegged losses even higher. Recent cases span a French kidnapping in which workers’ children were held hostage and a UK home invasion that ended in prison terms for the attackers.

The sentencing offers one of the clearest signals yet that U.S. courts are treating crypto wrench attacks as serious violent crime.

Security researchers identified $9.17 million in frozen assets as the Brazilian exchange became the latest target in a wave of attacks following Binance's record $6.3 billion hack.

Tether has frozen more than $4.5 million in USDT linked to a security breach at Brazilian crypto exchange Mercado Bitcoin.

Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino confirmed the freeze on Nov. 2, saying the stablecoin issuer blocked more than 4.5 million USDT linked to the incident.

Notably, Tether is a major investor in the exchange. The stablecoin issuer announced a $20 million strategic investment in Mercado Bitcoin in July to support its expansion into tokenization, payments, and other digital financial services.

Meanwhile, on-chain analyst Specter reported that coordinated efforts involving security researchers and stablecoin issuers had expanded the immobilized assets to more than $9 million across nine digital assets, including USDC, PAXG, RLUSD, and others.

The intervention came as blockchain analytics firm Arkham Intelligence identified approximately $46 million in cryptocurrency held by wallets attributed to the attacker, including $8.37 million in Ethereum, $8.24 million in Bitcoin and $1.76 million in PEPE.

Earlier today, Mercado Bitcoin disclosed that it had identified and contained a security incident affecting one of its systems overnight.

Mercado Bitcoin subsequently published suspicious destination addresses across Bitcoin, Ethereum-compatible networks, Solana, Stellar and Tron to support tracing and potential recovery efforts.

The Mercado Bitcoin breach comes less than four days after hackers stole a record $6.3 billion from Binance on Oct. 29, extending a series of major attacks against centralized crypto exchanges.

Binance's incident followed a $388 million security breach at Bitget on Sept. 24, when attackers siphoned assets from the exchange's wallet infrastructure. Bitget subsequently tapped its protection fund to absorb the losses and protect customer balances.

The attacks have revived concerns about the security of centralized trading platforms, which collectively custody billions of dollars in digital assets and depend on internal systems to authorize transfers.

A similar pattern emerged in 2025, when two major exchanges suffered substantial losses within weeks of each other.

In February, Bybit lost approximately $1.5 billion after hackers manipulated the transaction approval process for one of its Ethereum cold wallets. The incident followed a $69 million hot-wallet breach at Phemex in January.

Although the incidents involved different attack methods, they exposed vulnerabilities in wallet management, transaction authorization, and the infrastructure exchanges rely on to safeguard customer assets.

The North Korean-linked TraderTraitor operation has been implicated in the two largest attacks. The FBI attributed both the Bybit and Binance thefts to North Korean hackers, demonstrating how sophisticated threat actors have repeatedly targeted centralized custodians.

However, investigators have not established any connection between those operations and the latest Mercado Bitcoin breach.

#5164. 8 Things That Should Always Be in Your Field Bag

Game day is only one part of an athlete’s schedule. These versatile picks from Brooks are made for the rest of your routine.

If you’re a regular at your local soccer league, you probably have your game-day uniform down to a science: cleats, socks, shorts, jersey, done. But you also know that training doesn’t end when you leave the field. There are warmups before practice, conditioning sessions, gym workouts, recovery afterwards, and, of course, the inevitable post-game team hangouts while you’re still wearing half your soccer gear. The right off-field pieces can make all of that a little more comfortable.

Brooks has plenty of options that can slot into those in-between moments—from cushioned running shoes for off-field training to lightweight layers for chilly practices to comfortable sweats for the ride home.

Below are eight of our favorite picks for the training, travel, and downtime surrounding the “beautiful game.”

The Glycerin 23 is arguably Brooks’ most versatile off-pitch training shoe. It’s perfect for road-running and training on hard surfaces thanks to plush cushioning and a smooth, stable ride that’s ideal for conditioning runs, or other training away from the field. The breathable upper and roomy fit also make it a comfortable option when you’re on your feet all day or logging miles without a ball at your feet.

For early-morning practices and chilly fall training sessions, lightweight layers that you can easily move in become essential. The Dash 1/2 Zip 3.0 is made with sweat-wicking fabric and has a semi-fitted silhouette that works over a training top without feeling too bulky or overbearing. Thumbholes help keep the sleeves in place, while a watch window lets you check your stats without needing to pull up your sleeve.

After practice, it’s natural to want to keep things comfy. The sweatpants have an incredibly soft brushed interior and an adjustable waistband, while the hoodie provides an extra layer when temperatures drop. You’ll never want to take this combo off.

If your warmup routine involves more than a few laps around the field, the Movement Tech Jogger is designed to keep up. These mid-rise bottoms have a 28-inch inseam, water-repellent fabric, and zippered pockets for all your essentials. Ankle zippers make it easier to get the pants on and off over shoes, which is particularly handy when you’re heading straight from the sidelines and into the game.

After kicking off your cleats post-game, the Adrenaline GTS 10 is an ideal recovery shoe. It’s a lifestyle take on Brooks’ longtime runner, reimagined from the 2009 model, with an open-air mesh upper and nitrogen-infused DNA TUNED cushioning. It’s an easy option for walking around after a game or practice, whether you’re heading home, meeting teammates for food, or running a few errands.

Sometimes the best post-practice top is simply one you don’t have to think about. This Graphic Short Sleeve has a relaxed fit and a soft cotton-polyester blend, making it a great choice after training or on a rest day. It’s also versatile enough for gym sessions and other low-key activities when you want something more casual and uncomplicated than your usual performance gear.

For outdoor training days when you need more coverage without piling on heavy layers, the Luxe Long Sleeve offers a truly useful middle ground. Its soft, breathable fabric has odor-resistant properties and UPF 50+ sun protection, while thumbholes help keep the sleeves in place. Wear it on its own during a cool-weather workout or underneath a jacket when temperatures really start to dip.

After spending 90 minutes running around in soccer socks, changing into a fresh pair can feel not only like a luxury, but a necessity. The Reset Crew Socks have a soft cotton blend, plush cushioning, a seamless toe, and arch and midfoot compression for a secure feel. An odor-resistant finish is another welcome feature, whether they’re going straight into your gym bag after practice or carrying you into the rest of your day.

#5163. Binance hackers begin swapping stolen Solana tokens for Bitcoin: Chainalysis

Crypto exchange Gate said it froze two linked accounts as US investigators urged platforms to block transactions tied to the $6.3 billion theft.

The hackers behind Binance’s $6.3 billion theft have begun converting stolen Solana tokens into Bitcoin after largely emptying the wallets used to launder funds on Tron, according to blockchain investigators.

Lookonchain reported Sunday that the hackers had moved 486,970 Solana (SOL) tokens, worth about $46.4 million, and were swapping them for Bitcoin (BTC) through Relay.

The activity involves funds that escaped the freezes imposed after Thursday’s theft, the largest in cryptocurrency history. Industry partners, including Tether and Circle, froze about $3 billion in stolen assets, while investigator SomaXBT estimated the attackers still controlled about $3.5 billion.

Binance said the attack compromised its hot wallets, with early findings pointing to a hacked employee laptop before investigators identified additional breach points. The exchange began restoring withdrawals Sunday, pledged to cover the losses and has been working with US authorities to trace and recover the stolen assets.

Related: OKX draws $445M in net inflows as Binance outflows exceed $7B

Chainalysis said Sunday that most of the hackers’ temporary holding wallets on Tron had been emptied as laundering activity expanded to Solana. It put the value of the Tron transfers at about $500 million.

The $500 million figure counted transfers during laundering, including repeated movements between wallets, SomaXBT said in response. About $242 million actually left the Tron holding wallets, he said.

Chainalysis said Friday that hackers may be using automation to obscure the trail, citing thousands of transactions in a short period. The firm observed funds circulating repeatedly between wallets, sometimes returning to addresses used earlier in the sequence.

Some stolen funds also reached centralized exchange Gate. Lookonchain reported Monday that the hackers had deposited about $250,000 there over the preceding 12 hours.

Gate subsequently said it had frozen two linked accounts and would cooperate with law enforcement. Its statement did not specify how much money was frozen.

The FBI on Saturday attributed Thursday’s theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor hackers and published wallet addresses linked to the stolen assets.

The agency, US Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation urged THORChain node operators, exchanges and decentralized finance (DeFi) services to block transactions involving those addresses or funds traced back to them.

Investigators had observed the hackers converting stolen assets primarily into Ether (ETH) and expected further laundering through DeFi and instant swap services, the FBI said.

#5162. Binance Hack: Why Bitcoin Didn't Crash Like It Did in 2018

Binance Hack: Why Bitcoin Didn't Crash Like It Did in 2018

Bitcoin is down about 4% a day after the biggest crypto hack on record. In March 2018, a failed attack on the same exchange knocked nearly 11% off its price in minutes, and Binance said at the time that no funds had been stolen.

Binance has confirmed yesterday's attack, and Chainalysis and TRM Labs put the theft at roughly $6.4 billion, more than four times the previous record hack: the $1.5 billion Bybit heist of February 2025. Bitcoin dipped to about $76,400 on Friday, around 6% below where it traded after Wednesday’s Federal Reserve decision.

More than $1.3 billion in leveraged bets was liquidated, meaning trades placed with borrowed money that exchanges close automatically when prices move against them. And yet Bitcoin is holding relatively steady, all things considered.

The 2018 incident was a phishing and theft attempt: attackers took over accounts, created API keys (credentials that let trading bots act on an account) and used them to pump the obscure coin Viacoin while 31 accounts that had pre-deposited the coin sold it. Bitcoin fell from $10,740 to $9,690 within minutes and kept dropping to about $6,600 by April 5, though the market was already in a bear run after peaking near $20,000 in December 2017.

To have a grasp of the situation, the entire crypto market was worth just over $400 billion in March 2018 and is worth roughly $2.6 trillion now.

A big reason for that, and why panic doesn't hit markets the same way anymore, is U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs. Funds like BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust let people buy Bitcoin through an ordinary brokerage account, and they now hold roughly 1.3 million BTC, about 6% of the supply.

Their shareholders don’t keep coins on Binance, and sovereign wealth funds such as Mubadala and the Abu Dhabi Investment Council have been buying. BlackRock’s fund alone took in $136 million on Wednesday, per Farside Investors data.

These funds don’t tend to panic sell so easily, and those funds remain locked for long periods of time.

The theft began at 4:05 p.m. ET Thursday, after U.S. markets closed, so Thursday’s preliminary $17 million of ETF inflows predate it and Friday’s flow figures are the first real read on whether those holders are selling.

The attacker still holds more than 420,000 ETH and 18,270 BTC, about $2.4 billion that no stablecoin issuer can freeze. The amount doesn’t account for other tokens, which would increase the holdings to more than $3 billion.

TRM and Chainalysis tie the attack to the North Korean group behind Bybit, which after that heist converted about 84% of the stolen Ethereum into Bitcoin through Thorchain, a cross-chain swap network.

Binance says it has set aside more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover every loss, and it is buying the missing tokens on the open market and over the counter, meaning in private deals off the exchange. About $3 billion is frozen, deposits are operating normally, and withdrawals are on track to resume in 45 hours.

Market sentiment was already soft before the theft and slid further: CoinMarketCap’s Fear and Greed index, a 0-to-100 gauge of market mood, dropped to 36 points from 43 (now in “fear” territory after being “neutral” yesterday), and Bitcoin sits about 38% below its $126,080 record. Back in 2018, the market was well in “extreme fear” territory at 12 points on the scale when the incident happened. Traders were already in panic mode, and the attack just worsened an already ugly situation.

Glassnode data show long-term holders underwater on about 4 million coins bought between $85,000 and $118,000, and HashKey analyst Tim Sun said before the hack that the market’s problem “is not panic selling, but rather insufficient new buying interest.”

So, taken all together, what it all boils down to is this: A more optimistic market, much more liquidity, active long-term investors, a clearer regulatory framework, a sense of safety thanks to that regulatory clarity, quick action by stablecoin providers, and a price trend in recovery likely all played a role in keeping Bitcoin safe from a global panic despite the record-breaking hack.

#5161. Binance warns of second wave of crypto theft as $6.3 billion hack recovery continues

The exchange has completed reserve verification for 10 cryptocurrencies but says scammers could exploit customers seeking withdrawals and compensation.

Binance has warned customers about potential scams exploiting withdrawal delays as the exchange recovers from a $6.3 billion security breach.

In a Nov. 2 security advisory, the exchange said fraudsters could take advantage of its phased withdrawal reopening by impersonating Binance representatives and offering customers assistance with delayed transactions, compensation claims and asset recovery.

The warning covers fraudulent emails, direct messages, group chats and even small cryptocurrency transfers carrying malicious instructions.

According to Binance, scammers may promise to speed up pending withdrawals, sell customers priority access to withdrawal queues, or instruct them to transfer their holdings into supposedly secure wallets.

The exchange emphasized that it does not charge fees to unlock withdrawals, offer paid recovery services or ask customers to authorize wallet transactions to regain access to their funds.

It also warned against fraudulent proof-of-reserves websites and compensation eligibility links, which could become particularly deceptive as the exchange introduces new verification tools following the breach.

Once customers approve malicious wallet permissions, attackers can transfer their assets without further authorization, potentially creating losses that cannot be reversed.

The warning comes as Binance attempts to restore normal operations after an Oct. 29 attack that compromised its hot wallets and resulted in approximately $6.3 billion in stolen cryptocurrencies.

Meanwhile, Binance announced on Nov. 2 that it had completed the zero-knowledge proof for its Oct. 31 reserve snapshot, allowing customers to independently verify the backing of ten major cryptocurrencies.

The covered assets include Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB, XRP, Solana, Zcash, and four stablecoins: USDT, USDC, USD1, and RLUSD.

Binance said the completed proof lets customers verify that their balances were included in the snapshot and backed by reserves of at least 1:1, without revealing individual account holdings.

The process requires users to obtain account-specific verification information and download a verification tool through Binance's official proof-of-reserves platform.

However, the verification applies to balances recorded at 00:00 UTC on Oct. 31 and does not establish the exchange's current financial position or independently audit its overall solvency.

The announcement also comes as Binance continues replenishing assets affected by the theft.

According to the exchange, approximately 95% of the impacted assets have been replaced using company resources, while the remaining 5% consists of less-liquid cryptocurrencies that are more difficult to acquire in sufficient quantities.

Binance has been sourcing those assets through market purchases and over-the-counter transactions, separately from efforts to trace and recover the original stolen funds.

The exchange began restoring withdrawals on Nov. 1, with access returning progressively across supported cryptocurrencies and blockchain networks.

Another phase is scheduled for Nov. 3, although Binance has yet to confirm which additional assets and networks will become available.

The prolonged reopening gives fraudsters an opportunity to exploit customers awaiting access to their funds, particularly through fake support channels and requests for wallet authorizations.

Binance has instructed customers with pending withdrawals to check their status directly through its application and verify suspicious communications using its official verification service.

The exchange plans to publish another reserve snapshot on Nov. 4 covering additional cryptocurrencies. Generating the accompanying zero-knowledge proof is expected to take another 40 to 50 hours.

#5158. Reddit Stock Plunges 30% as Google's AI Search Hits Traffic and User Growth

Reddit Stock Plunges 30% as Google's AI Search Hits Traffic and User Growth

Reddit shares plunged 30.44% to $90.15 on Friday after CEO Steve Huffman warned that Google's AI-powered search features are cutting referral traffic and could shrink the platform's user base.

The selloff came after the company reported strong third-quarter results but issued a weaker-than-expected revenue forecast for the current quarter.

Reddit built much of its business around people discovering its discussions through Google searches, and those visitors are increasingly finding answers without ever clicking through to the platform. That puts pressure on the advertising business that has helped turn Reddit into one of the internet's fastest-growing publicly traded companies.

Reddit's third-quarter numbers initially looked healthy. Revenue climbed 53% year over year to $895 million, advertising revenue increased 54% to $847 million, and net income reached $283 million. Diluted earnings per share, which measure company profit attributable to each share while accounting for potential dilution, came in at $1.40, up 75% from a year earlier and above the $1.33 analyst consensus.

But the audience figures were less encouraging since Reddit reported 130.3 million daily active unique visitors, up 12% year over year but below the roughly 134 million analysts expected. In the U.S., the number actually fell 2% to 50.7 million, giving investors another reason to question whether the platform can maintain its growth.

Huffman delivered the warning during Thursday's earnings call, explaining that Google search referrals had fallen by more than one million on average every week during October, with the decline accelerating toward the end of the third quarter. If that pace continues, Reddit's total daily active users could fall by a low double-digit percentage in Q4 from the current base of around 130 million.

Huffman pointed directly at Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode, features that generate answers and summaries directly inside search results. Rather than sending users to websites to find information, Google increasingly gives them what they are looking for on its own page, pushing traditional search links further down.

Asked whether the changes were responsible for Reddit's declining search traffic, Huffman said the AI features had expanded aggressively in the U.S. and internationally. "The AI mode does not drive traffic, not for us and not to anybody as far as I know," he told investors.

That creates an awkward situation for Reddit—and arguably every other single media site on the internet. People can still search for Reddit discussions, but Google's results increasingly allow them to consume information from those discussions without visiting Reddit itself. Search referrals also bring back existing users, meaning fewer clicks can affect both new-user acquisition and the platform's ability to keep people engaged.

Reddit is trying to reduce that dependence by moving toward a primarily logged-in experience, which would require people to sign into an account before accessing most of the platform. The company plans to begin testing the change in selected markets outside the U.S. during the fourth quarter.

The strategy also connects to Reddit's increasingly important relationship with the AI industry. In February 2024, Reddit signed a reported $60 million-a-year data licensing deal with Google, giving the search giant access to Reddit discussions to train AI models. A few months later, the company announced a similar partnership with OpenAI, allowing the ChatGPT developer to use Reddit content while giving Reddit access to OpenAI's technology.

Those deals turned Reddit's enormous archive of human conversations into something it could sell to AI developers. But the same AI-powered search experience that benefits from Reddit's content can reduce the number of people who actually visit the site. Reddit also started tightening access to its public data and moving toward a more restricted platform which angered long term users.

The stock has now lost 44% over the past week, with Friday's 30.44% plunge accounting for a significant portion of the decline. At $90.15, Reddit is trading well below the levels it held just days ago.

The technical picture offers little immediate relief. Reddit's 50-day exponential moving average, a trend indicator that gives greater weight to recent prices, sits around $149.80, while its 200-day average is near $162.12. The 50-day average has already fallen below the 200-day average, creating a so-called death cross, a bearish signal commonly associated with a longer-term downward trend.

At $90.15, Reddit would need to climb approximately 66%—almost 70%—just to return to its 50-day average. That would only bring the share price back to the shorter-term trend line, not undo the death cross itself. With both averages sitting far above the current price, a recovery to those levels in the near term looks increasingly unlikely.

#5157. Binance can cut a winning Bitcoin hedge even when customer assets are backed

Binance says only surplus futures reserves were reallocated, while ADL rules can still reduce an opposing profitable position.

Binance's latest reserve proof addresses whether a customer's Bitcoin is backed at a dated snapshot. A futures hedge faces a separate test: Binance's futures rules allow Auto-Deleveraging, or ADL, to reduce a profitable short that was offsetting the holding.

In its Nov. 2 proof-completion update, Binance said holders of ten named tokens, including Bitcoin, could independently verify backing of at least 1:1 for the snapshot taken at 00:00 UTC on Oct. 31.

The exchange had disclosed in its Oct. 31 recovery update that some futures insurance reserves helped replenish assets stolen in its security incident. Binance said it released only excess above its required coverage level and that the remaining funds exceeded that requirement. The disclosure alone establishes neither a reserve shortfall nor a measurable increase in ADL probability.

Binance also distinguished its Futures Insurance Funds from user assets: they are its own reserves, outside the user-verifiable PoR view. Those reserves support the handling of bankrupt futures positions and reduce the need to close opposing traders' positions.

Binance said it monitors those funds against stress scenarios and adds company funds when required.

The futures insurance FAQ describes several pools assigned to different contract categories, with Binance able to change allocations. An exchange-wide reserve figure therefore cannot automatically describe the protection available to every Bitcoin contract.

The same FAQ defines Maximum Takeover Capacity as a cap on the notional, or face, value of bankrupt positions a fund can absorb at a time. It is a multiple of the fund's current balance, with the predetermined multiplier kept confidential.

That capacity limit differs from the amount available to absorb losses. Its FAQ says ADL can be engaged when takeover capacity is reached or when unrealized losses on positions assumed by the fund exceed the relevant available balance. Waiting for a fund balance to reach zero would miss the capacity constraint described in its guidance.

Neither the amount released nor the information needed to calculate current contract-specific headroom is established by the reallocation disclosure.

Under the ADL priority rules, opposing profitable positions can be selected when the fund cannot accept a bankrupt position. Profitability and leverage affect their place in the queue. A position can therefore be winning on price and still be selected for reduction.

Consider a purely hypothetical trader holding 1 BTC and a linear futures short of 1 BTC. Assume the short has become profitable after a price decline. If ADL cuts it to 0.5 BTC while the underlying holding stays unchanged, only half the holding remains offset.

If Bitcoin then falls by an assumed $10,000 per BTC, the remaining combined position loses $5,000 on that further move. That calculation assumes spot and futures move together, quantities remain fixed and the trader adds no replacement hedge. It excludes fees, funding, basis differences, taxes and collateral changes.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

The $5,000 is an incremental loss after the reduction, not the strategy's total profit or loss. Whatever the closed portion earned does not provide an ongoing offset to later price changes in the holding.

For positions governed by Binance RCH's clearing rules, an ADL-selected position can be reduced or closed at the triggering bankrupt position's bankruptcy price, without specific consent from the affected clearing participant.

This differs from the collateral problem in CryptoSlate's October analysis of fragmented hedges, where an underfunded losing leg can be liquidated while profits sit elsewhere. ADL can remove the profitable opposing leg. Either mechanism can separate positions that were intended to work together.

Binance's Delta Neutral Account guidance offers qualifying hedged positions lower ADL priority within the same profit/loss category. It does not exempt those positions from ADL.

Initial qualification requires Portfolio Margin or Portfolio Margin Pro, VIP4 or above and an enabled Delta Mode for the individual account. The gap between the calculated long and short exposures must be less than 5% of the larger side, expressed as a relative difference below 0.05. Enabling a master account does not enable its subaccounts.

The calculation recognizes eligible assets in Cross Margin and Futures accounts, Cross Margin debts and futures positions. Assets in the Spot Account and options positions are excluded. A Bitcoin holding and an offsetting futures short may form an economic hedge without automatically qualifying for this special queue treatment.

There is also a distinction between entry and continuing eligibility: the FAQ says a later fall below VIP4 alone changes nothing, while disabling Portfolio Margin disables Delta Mode.

Contract scope matters alongside account status. Within the Binance RCH rulebook, ADL applies contract by contract: a position in one contract type is not used to cover losses in another. Those rules refer to Default Funds and tie potentially affected positions to the relevant fund's coverage and available capacity.

The FAQs are educational guidance that defer to governing rules and contract specifications. The applicable Binance entity, product terms and account arrangement determine which legal protections govern a position.

#5155. FATF targets crypto hubs in review of money laundering controls

The watchdog has not named the jurisdictions under review. Initial findings on compliance with its crypto standards are due in June 2027.

The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) is launching a targeted review of jurisdictions with significant crypto activity to address gaps in how governments apply global anti-money laundering standards.

On Friday, the FATF, an intergovernmental body that sets global standards to combat money laundering, announced that the review would focus primarily on jurisdictions with “materially important” virtual asset service provider (VASP) activity, taking their existing assessment status into account.

The watchdog said its regular assessments and follow-up procedures would remain the main tools for evaluating compliance.

Initial findings will be published in June 2027, with further results in October 2027. The review will also be followed by monitoring and faster reporting to track progress in addressing deficiencies.

The FATF did not name the jurisdictions it would review or say how many would be included. Cointelegraph contacted the watchdog for further details but had not received a response by publication.

The move follows a July FATF report showing that 83% of surveyed jurisdictions had adopted crypto Travel Rule legislation, while significant enforcement gaps persisted.

The report found that 55 of the 91 jurisdictions with Travel Rule laws had yet to take supervisory or enforcement action over compliance. Authorities also struggled to identify unlicensed crypto businesses and oversee providers serving local customers from overseas.

The Travel Rule requires crypto service providers to share information about the sender and recipient of transfers.

Related: FATF urges faster crypto AML enforcement as stablecoin crime increases

#5154. Worried About Crypto Hacks? Buy Bitcoin Proxies in Stock Market Instead, Say Wall Street Firms

Worried About Crypto Hacks? Buy Bitcoin Proxies in Stock Market Instead, Say Wall Street Firms

Wall Street analysts are telling clients the record-breaking hack of Binance is a buying opportunity, not a reason to flee, urging investors to scoop up crypto-linked stocks while prices are depressed.

Analysts at Cantor Fitzgerald, TD Cowen, and Compass Point said in Friday research notes that the roughly $6.3 billion theft, the largest crypto hack ever, is unlikely to derail the broader market’s recovery.

The reassurance came a day after the exploit rattled markets and sent Bitcoin sliding toward $77,000.

Cantor’s Ramsey El-Assal pointed to how fast the industry moved to contain the damage, noting that stablecoin issuers and others froze roughly $3 billion of the stolen funds, with Tether freezing more than $1.5 billion, Circle about $800 million and Ripple around $200 million.

El-Assal expects shares of Coinbase, Robinhood, and Strategy to recover once the panic fades. “We would be buyers on weakness,” he wrote, adding that while the episode is painful, “this is not 2022.”

TD Cowen’s Lance Vitanza struck a similar note, arguing the breach exposed weaknesses in Binance’s own security rather than in the underlying technology behind Bitcoin, and framing the selloff as a chance to add to Bitcoin and the stocks of public companies that hold it.

Compass Point’s Ed Engel and Michael Donovan said Binance has “more than enough liquidity to cover the hole,” while flagging that reimbursing customers could strain stablecoin supply and that rivals like Coinbase and Hyperliquid could pick up business. They are watching the $75,000 to $77,000 Bitcoin range as a key level.

The logic behind buying stocks over tokens is that regulated, exchange-listed proxies like Coinbase, Robinhood, and Strategy offer crypto exposure without the custody risk the hack laid bare, and tend to rebound once sentiment steadies.

Not everyone is sanguine. Cristiano Ventricelli, vice president of digital assets at Moody’s Ratings, said the incident “underscores the heightened cybersecurity risks associated with hot wallets” and “illustrates the risk concentration inherent in large, centralized intermediaries.”

He cautioned that the broader implications will hinge on “the ultimate losses, affected counterparties, asset recovery, and importantly, whether the incident leads to wider disruption or loss of confidence.”

Binance has set aside $6.34 billion to cover losses and told users their assets are safe, while the Secret Service and FBI have opened a probe and firms including TRM and Chainalysis have tied the hack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group.

#5153. Kinetic’s $24 million XRP-linked lending market showed a 0.04% base rate before rewards

Kinetic’s November 1 snapshots separate modest FXRP loan demand from collateral use and incentive-supported returns.

Kinetic’s FXRP lending market on Flare showed roughly $24 million supplied on Nov. 1, yet the base annualized rate for lenders was about 0.04% before rewards. For XRP holders, the supplied balance alone is a weak measure of borrower-funded income.

Kinetic is a lending protocol on Flare, where FXRP represents XRP-linked exposure through the FAssets system. Its official market page displayed $24 million of FXRP supplied and $2 million borrowed in the Nov. 1 observation.

The paired stablecoin market told a different story. FlareSignal’s Nov. 1 lending snapshot put FXRP utilization at 6.7%, against 92.8% for USDT0. The gap helps explain why demand to borrow a token, demand to borrow against it, and the income paid to its holders require separate measures.

The FXRP supply APR in that snapshot was about 0.04%, while the FXRP borrower APR was about 0.7%. The supply figure describes a simple annualized base rate at the observation time.

Rewards change the displayed return. In the Nov. 1 capture, Kinetic’s official FXRP row showed a 0.59% supply APY and a separately displayed 0.55% rFLR reward component. The reward component belongs inside the quoted yield comparison; adding it again to the headline supply APY would overstate the display.

DefiLlama’s specific isoFXRP pool page separately labeled its 0.57% supply APY as a 30-day average, alongside a 0.04% base component and a +0.54% reward component labeled WFLR. Rounding and differing observation windows limit direct reconciliation with the app’s figures.

DefiLlama’s Kinetic adapter calculates base yield from supply rates and rewards from separate emissions and token prices. That separation identifies the economic question behind the headline: how much comes from borrowers paying for credit, and how much comes from incentive distributions? The observed reward component was much larger than the quoted base rate.

FlareSignal reported about 19.45 million FXRP supplied and 1.31 million FXRP borrowed in the dated observation. It also reported about 5.04 million USDT0 supplied and 4.68 million USDT0 borrowed. The utilization figures show substantially different demand for borrowing the two assets within the isolated market.

Supplied FXRP may also support borrowing when enabled as collateral and permitted by market rules. Kinetic’s lending documentation describes suppliers enabling assets as collateral to borrow other assets, with borrowers required to remain overcollateralized. Someone seeking stablecoin liquidity may value an XRP-linked collateral position while having little use for an additional FXRP loan.

Collateral utility gives the holder access to borrowing. Any cash return to a supplier remains a separate benefit. A holder may value access to credit while receiving little base interest on the supplied asset.

The USDT0 figure reports aggregate market debt. Kinetic’s isolated-market contract directory identifies the market’s assets and infrastructure, but attributing that debt to FXRP collateral requires individual account data.

XRP is the XRP Ledger’s native asset, while the asset supplied to this Kinetic market is FXRP on Flare. That distinction places additional protocol steps between holding native XRP and having a lending position.

Flare’s XRP minting documentation describes sending underlying XRP to the Core Vault on the XRP Ledger, followed by an executor finalizing the FXRP mint on Flare using verified payment evidence. The FAssets system connects that representation to underlying assets and collateral arrangements.

The return journey has conditions too. Under the ordinary holder redemption process, FAssets are burned and underlying payment is initiated through the protocol. Fees and redemption-ticket limits can apply. If an agent fails to pay, compensation can involve collateral after proof of nonpayment.

Kinetic’s Nov. 1 observations show substantial FXRP supplied relative to FXRP loans, with a reward component much larger than base lender interest. For this lending market, the test for lasting demand is continued use of credit and the interest borrowers pay for it. The supplied balance establishes market size; those cash flows would establish a stronger foundation for lender income.

#5151. Coinbase (COIN) Misses Revenue Estimates as Users Fall, Armstrong Sets Up New Share Sales

Coinbase missed revenue expectations as users declined, despite growth in recurring revenue, while executive share-sale plans and a massive Binance security breach added pressure to crypto markets.

Coinbase had a mixed third quarter. Revenue came in at $1.20 billion, below the $1.233 billion analysts expected, according to company filings. Subscription and services revenue did better, reaching $570 million. The company is still heavily tied to trading activity, but its recurring income is growing.

Monthly Transacting Users fell to 7.4 million, down from 9.3 million a year earlier. During its earnings call, Coinbase blamed overall market conditions. Its share of crypto trading volume did rise to 10.7%, the fourth straight quarter of gains, which suggests it is winning business even as the broader market quiets.

JUST IN: Coinbase disclosed buying 643 Bitcoin worth $1.5 billion for its balance sheet in Q3 🚀 pic.twitter.com/5BYdrwLCJN

Separately, filings reported on October 30 show CEO Brian Armstrong has set up a plan to sell up to 8.17 million Class A shares. He adopted the plan in August under SEC Rule 10b5-1, which lets executives schedule sales ahead of time. Sales could run from November 16 through October 2027, subject to stock price conditions. Co-founder Fred Ehrsam and President Emilie Choi have similar plans, bringing the total to about 13.6 million shares.

This is not new territory for Armstrong. In the past, VanEck analyst Matthew Sigel tracked about $545.7 million in sales over nine months, starting in April 2025. Armstrong has said these sales are part of his risk management, not a signal about the company.

Coinbase shares (COIN) fell about 15% today, but not necessarily due to this earnings report.

Binance disclosed a security breach on October 29 that it estimates at $6.3 billion, making it the largest crypto theft on record. Around $3 billion in assets has been frozen so far, with industry partners assisting in the freezes.

The hackers are allegedly linked to North Korea, though Binance has not attributed the attack to any group. The exchange says it has found no evidence of a leaked wallet private key.

Binance says it has $6.34 billion in reserves available to cover losses. Deposits were unaffected, and the company expects to resume withdrawals within 48 hours. Figures remain preliminary, and estimates vary slightly across outlets.

The market reacted quickly. Bitcoin fell roughly 4.5% to below $77,000. Shares of Strategy (MSTR) fell nearly 10% on the day. Strive (ASST) shares fell over 12% at times. Coinbase’s stock is down over 55% on the year.

#5150. Ethena’s trading team can approve borrowers of assets backing USDe under new rules

The October 29 framework delegates qualifying borrower screening while retaining committee call-in powers and oversight of lending limits.

Ethena’s October 29 institutional-lending framework sets out a route for its trading team to onboard qualifying borrowers of assets backing USDe without an individual Risk Committee vote.

The posted rules describe a change in approval authority over lending that helps back Ethena’s synthetic dollar. For USDe holders, published eligibility rules and exposure disclosures offer a way to assess that credit risk. The committee retains oversight, with borrower documents sent to it privately.

The framework posted by Kairos Research describes the delegated route; it identifies no newly funded borrower using it.

Eligibility combines bilateral lending with full recourse to the borrower or a parent guarantee, jurisdiction and standing checks, sanctions screening, segregated tri-party custody and verifiable daily collateral reports. The custody arrangement puts collateral with a third party.

Borrower documents go privately to the committee at least three business days before first funding. A member calling a borrower in must identify a failed criterion, with a decision within five business days. The committee therefore retains a criterion-based call-in power, while the text leaves funding during a pending objection unspecified. Cases outside the framework still require committee review.

The lending team sets loan-to-value rate cards, shared monthly with the committee alongside book reporting. Loan-to-value measures the amount lent relative to collateral value. A missed margin call, default or changed standing stops new lending to that counterparty and triggers escalation within 48 hours.

The permitted collateral includes BTC, ETH and other specified assets. USDe, sUSDe, ENA, USDtb and borrowers’ own assets are excluded; Ethereum-based XAUT is conditional on custody, liquidation venues and a weekend liquidation test.

The framework preserves five existing approvals. Its public text sets no numerical aggregate lending cap or per-borrower concentration ceiling.

Ethena’s institutional-lending documentation places aggregate exposure limits under governance and committee review, without publishing a numerical ceiling.

The earlier partner-by-partner approach is visible in the March 10 Maple and Anchorage proposal. It said additional offchain partners would need new proposals to the Risk Committee. LlamaRisk, Kairos Research and Blockworks Advisory subsequently posted support for the reviewed agreements.

Those reviews already kept contractual terms confidential. The October development concerns approval authority; confidentiality predates it.

The March discussion also shows why a partner’s brand is insufficient to identify the legal claim. Anchorage’s agreement was with A1, Ltd., a Cayman Islands group entity distinct from the OCC-chartered Anchorage Digital Bank. Maple’s pool-based agreement ran through Delaware’s Protocol Pool Operations Alpha LLC.

LlamaRisk’s April legal-review methodology names Ethena (BVI) Limited as the entity deploying reserve-backing assets. It examines collateral ratios, custody segregation, perfected security interests, liquidation rights, recall and redelivery timing, and practical enforceability.

The signing entity and contract matter because they govern the claim on borrowed assets and collateral.

Retaining the five existing approvals preserves arrangements with different structures; it does not establish that every legacy pool or warehouse meets the new bilateral criteria. LlamaRisk’s August 4 FalconX review described warehouse financing to FalconX International Lending Opportunities SPC for its segregated portfolio SP 1. The vehicle acquires institutional loan receivables and pledges its assets to Ethena, rather than operating as an ordinary bilateral borrower.

FalconX then announced a $1 billion secured SPV facility on August 19. That was an announced financing capacity, not a verified outstanding loan balance on November 1.

LlamaRisk’s October 12 assessment allocated 14.3% of backing to institutional lending, against total reported backing of roughly $5 billion and a similar USDe supply.

Blockworks Advisory’s Q3 governance update, published October 13, put institutional lending at 8% of liquid cash as of September 30. The two percentages use different dates and denominators. Comparing them as a rise from 8% to 14.3% would therefore be misleading.

CryptoSlate’s earlier lending analysis examined how allocations and recovery terms affect redemption liquidity. The October framework adds the question of which borrowers may enter through delegated screening.

Ethena’s lending dashboard describes collateral held with custodians, continuous LTV monitoring and no rehypothecation, meaning collateral is not pledged onward. In the November 1 text capture available for this report, borrower rows and the update time were unpopulated. It therefore provides no current borrower-level exposure or collateral ratios.

For holders, a usable assessment would put those elements together: the signing entity, its current outstanding amount, collateral and LTV, concentration against the relevant limit, and information to assess enforceability and recovery prospects.

#5149. The 2026 Unofficial Marathon Awards, According to an Editor Running New York City

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

This is the gear you actually need to make it to 26.2.

Last year, when I trained for my first marathon, I went a bit gear-crazy. I searched high and low for all the best products to help me get through training and across the finish line. And, I had a lot of fun doing it. I tested out dozens of sneakers, agonized over my race day outfit, and indulged in all the high-tech recovery gadgets (I have a recovery tool for basically every part of my body, from head to toe).

This year, my approach to gear is a lot simpler because I know what I like. More importantly, I know what works. For example: I’m going on two training cycles now of exclusively using Gu Raspberry Lemonade gels as my fuel on long runs. Yeah, when something is good, I’m dedicated.

So, while some of my training staple top spots haven’t budged—like my Bombas running socks, Garmin Forerunner 570, and Therabody JetBoots Pro Plus—that just means the things in this year’s Marathon Awards really impressed me.

I’m still loyal to many of the products in last year’s roundup of my faves, but these are the new additions that deserve a spot on the list.

I have been pretty dead-set on my Nike Vomero Plus (which I wore throughout training and on race day last year) as my max cushioned shoe for everyday runs for a while—but these sneaks from Hoka finally gave them some competition for that spot. They’re less pillowy and more structured, so I feel more in control on a run, and my heel and ankle have more support. During training this time around, I found that my feet started to crave a bit more of that stability from a shoe, so I switched over to the Cliftons to get me through my peak mileage. They hold their own on easy and long runs when it comes to comfort, and feel even better than the Nikes when I’m doing my speed intervals on the track.

There comes a point in training when I simply cannot get myself to wear anything but sneakers. My feet and body just need the support, even at work or running errands or going out with friends. The new Eliot Ryder from Tracksmith is a pillowy soft shoe that cushions every step. Made for running, it could totally double as your easy run go-to, but I’ve been living in it outside of logging miles as well. The shoe’s design also makes it a little more fashionable than other max-cushioned trainers that scream “running shoe.”

Recovery slides are definitely new for my training this year. After dealing with some mysterious foot aches and pains this time around, I started to wear slides around my apartment to avoid walking around flat-footed. Compared to others I tried, these are the softest and offer the most arch support.

I ran my favorite half marathon to date (the Lululemon SeaWheeze half) in this tank—so I’m a little sentimental. But still: it has the classic soft and breathable material I love Lululemon for, it’s super comfortable and lightweight over long distances, and comes in bright colors that will get you spotted on the course. I’m very much considering ironing my name onto the one I have and wearing it on race day.

I trained during the summer months in New York City, so a lightweight top was critical. This one from Salomon kept me comfortable throughout training (and also has a really cool, elevated look). I cannot stress enough just how lightweight, breathable, and quick-drying this fabric is. Truly a gem of a find!

Now that the weather is cooling down, this top from Rhone is my favorite for an early fall day. The material is soft and breathable, making it a perfect transition layer. And, I think the crop and mesh design make it cuter than other running long sleeves.

I would say the biggest thing I didn’t nail down last year was a running vest, so I’m excited to share that I’ve got one that I loved this time around. The big problem with last year’s (unnamed) vest is that the water bottles were always popping out. They stay put in this one from Hoka, which also feels lightweight and easily stores everything I need to bring with me. The closures are easy to work, it feels really secure and comfortable across long distances, and I like the pop the purple gives my usually all-black running outfit.

When all my laundry is clean, these are the first pair of shorts I grab above every other option. The main reason: I want to be comfortable on a run, and these are the most comfortable shorts I have by far. They don’t ride up, provide compression—but not too much compression—and have a softer feel. They have two pockets along the back (one zippered, where I keep my keys) and a mesh one (where I throw my empty gels), plus one on the right thigh (where I keep my phone).

This pair from Bandit also hits all the important notes in running shorts: they don’t ride up, offer compression, and are comfortable even on double-digit mile runs. These shorts also have extra grippy material inside to help them stay put and have pockets on both thighs and two along the back center, which is helpful if you have more things to carry with you on a run. (Come race day, when I don’t plan to wear a vest because I won’t need to carry my own water supply, I’m going to be happy to have an extra pocket to hold my gels!)

Lululemon’s low-impact Flow Y bra got an upgrade to be more supportive for higher-impact activities. The racerback bra has a mesh panel along the back too, making it more breathable on hot days. While training through the summer, I mostly end up running in just a sports bra, and this one also has a fun pattern to show off.

It’s very hard to successfully cross a finish line without the help of a training program. This year, I worked with Kelly Roberts, an RRCA-certified run coach and creator of the Badass Lady Gang. It’s a run community, and now, an app where you can get customized training programs, connect with Kelly and other runners, and utilize strength training, fueling, mindset, and recovery resources. It’s the most thorough platform I’ve ever seen, and Kelly was there to help me navigate the highs (5 and 10K PRs when I wasn’t even trying) and lows (strep throat) that popped up during training.

Bose just dropped these earbuds and I’ve been obsessed ever since I got my hands on them. They stay secure on your ears and have that open ear feature so you can still hear everything around you. But, since they’re Bose, the sound also feels more high quality than other options, and they’re slightly louder for moments when you really need to pump those tunes.

I love these sunglasses from Warby Parker Sport. They’re lightweight, but still feel like a solid, nice pair of sunglasses, and their look feels a little more elevated than some of the aggressively big and bold sunglasses that runners have to choose from. They also stay on my face, rain, shine, or sweat.

Not to be dramatic, but these hair ties from Goody changed my life. Last year, I watched a bunch of tutorials of how different influencers styled their hair for a race and purchased different products that would hopefully help tame my flyaways and often-drooping ponytail to no avail. It turns out, all I needed were these hair ties. They’re thicker and stronger than the regular old ones I’ve been wearing since I was a kid, and seem impossible to break. I can run for miles now and my hair doesn’t budge. I don’t know what kind of magic is in these things, but I’m grateful.

I don’t love the way most sunscreens sit on my skin, but obviously, some SPF is important when you’re spending that much time in the sun. I actually like this sunscreen from Summer Fridays—it melts into my skin, keeps me covered, and doesn’t get into my eyes when I’m on a run.

If you’re acne-prone like me, all that running and sweating that comes with marathon training could do a number on your skin. This year, I got in the habit of immediately rinsing my face with water once I got back to my apartment and then spraying it with Tower 28’s SOS spray for good measure. So far, no major breakouts to report.

#5147. Intel Stock Suffers Worst Crash in 50 Years as Weak Forecast Overshadows AI Chip Demand

Intel Stock Suffers Worst Crash in 50 Years as Weak Forecast Overshadows AI Chip Demand

Intel shares plunged nearly 30% to $65.76 on Friday after the chipmaker issued a fourth-quarter forecast that fell well short of Wall Street expectations, overshadowing an otherwise strong earnings report.

The selloff wiped out more than $146 billion in market value, and translated into the worst single-day decline in more than 50 years.

The problem is that Intel finds itself in an unusual position: demand for its processors is booming because of the AI infrastructure buildout, but the company cannot manufacture enough chips to capitalize on it. At the same time, its traditional PC business is struggling, and the factories needed to support its long-term recovery are consuming enormous amounts of money.

Intel's third-quarter numbers were actually quite good. Revenue climbed 21% year over year to $16.5 billion, while adjusted earnings per share reached $0.52, beating the company's guidance of $0.38 and Wall Street's $0.40 estimate. It was the company's eighth consecutive quarter of exceeding its financial expectations, according to CFO Dave Zinsner.

The strongest performer was Intel's Data Center and AI division, which generated $7.3 billion in revenue, up 78% year over year and nearly 80% compared with the same period last year. The division's operating profit reached $3 billion, representing 42% of its revenue.

But investors were looking at what comes next. Intel expects fourth-quarter revenue between $15 billion and $16 billion, meaning its midpoint guidance of $15.5 billion is roughly $1.6 billion below the $17.07 billion analysts had anticipated. Adjusted earnings per share are expected to fall to $0.25, compared with Wall Street's $0.43 estimate.

Gross margins, which measure how much revenue remains after accounting for the direct costs of making products, are also expected to deteriorate. Intel forecast a non-GAAP gross margin of 38% for Q4, down from 44.1% in the third quarter.

Three problems explain much of that deterioration: weaker PC demand, manufacturing constraints affecting server processors, and an accident at one of Intel's factories in Israel.

Intel CFO Dave Zinsner described 2027 as an investment year and warned investors not to expect positive free cash flow. Free cash flow is the money a company has left after paying operating expenses and investments in equipment and infrastructure. Intel expects to sacrifice cash generation in the short term to finance its manufacturing expansion.

"Probably not a dynamic where we are going to have positive free cash flow next year," Zinsner said during the earnings call. He added that Intel expects a return on invested capital of at least 20% on its manufacturing node investments, but acknowledged that several major projects will require substantial spending at the same time.

That spending is part of Intel's broader attempt to rebuild its manufacturing business and compete with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, or TSMC, the world's leading contract chipmaker. Intel wants to manufacture chips not only for its own products but also for outside customers, a business model known as a foundry.

The turnaround has attracted major partners. In September 2025, Nvidia invested $5 billion in Intel and agreed to collaborate on custom processors for PCs and data centers. The partnership gave Intel a financial boost while connecting its processors to Nvidia's AI ecosystem.

Intel's next-generation 18A process, the manufacturing technology behind chips such as Panther Lake, is central to the company's attempt to regain its technological edge.

More recently, a preliminary agreement with Apple to manufacture some of its chips helped send Intel shares above $130 in May. The potential deal could give Intel a significant new customer as Apple looks to diversify its manufacturing supply chain.

Those developments helped fuel optimism around Intel's recovery, but Friday's selloff shows how much still needs to go right. The company has strong demand in its data center business, yet it must increase manufacturing output, navigate a shrinking PC market and finance an expensive expansion before investors can expect consistent cash generation.
